This enables the analysis of completely different quantum experiments within a single framework.
tldr: The paper proposes using the average minimal Hamming distance of measurement bitstrings as a metric to characterize quantum states and detect phase transitions from limited data.
motivation: Quantum measurement data is often sparse relative to the exponentially large Hilbert space, limiting characterization. The authors aim to develop a robust metric that works with limited statistics.
method: They define the average minimal Hamming distance for a set of unique bitstrings and analyze its scaling behavior across various quantum experiments and simulations, including noisy processors, cold-atom simulators, and neural-network states.
result: The metric exhibits universal power-law behavior, and its parameters reliably capture state complexity and identify quantum phase transitions without extensive statistics or explicit observable calculations.
conclusion: The approach provides a unified framework for analyzing diverse quantum experiments, but its direct relevance to the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is limited.

title: Circuit-Level Noise Estimation Via Shuttling In Plaquette Circuits
authors: Alexandru Paler Huyen Do
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method for estimating QEC circuit-level noise levels assuming that only single-shot measurements are available (e.g. measurements are slow and performed in a zoned/parallel fashion), and that lower level quantum hardware calibration is not possible (e.g. cloud access) or not feasible (e.g. large scale computing). We develop and run surface code plaquette experiments using two syndrome qubit configurations: FRESH, involving fresh qubits for each plaquette repetition, and RECYCLE, reusing qubits. To validate our approach, we compile plaquettes to ion-trap (IonQ Aria1) native gate set and apply hardware-aware rewrite templates to reduce circuit depth and execution time. We also run the experiments on a non-shuttling, superconducting processor (IBM Torino). We estimate circuit-level noise rates from the resulting single-shot plaquette measurement statistics, and conclude numerically about the viability of low-depth QEC experiments.
tldr: This paper presents a method to estimate circuit-level noise in quantum error correction plaquette experiments using only single-shot measurements, without hardware calibration.
motivation: To enable noise estimation in QEC experiments when direct hardware calibration is unavailable or infeasible, such as in cloud access or large-scale systems.
method: Surface code plaquette experiments are run with two syndrome qubit configurations (FRESH and RECYCLE), compiled to ion-trap and superconducting processors, and noise rates are estimated from single-shot measurement statistics.
result: The method successfully estimates circuit-level noise rates and demonstrates viability of low-depth QEC experiments on both ion-trap and superconducting hardware.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for noise characterization in QEC without requiring low-level calibration, potentially aiding in scalable quantum computing.

title: Higher-order Exceptional Points In A Multimode Continuum Optoacoustic System
authors: Anton Montag, Julius T. Gohsrich, Quentin Levoy, Birgit Stiller, Flore K. Kunst
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exceptional points appear in non-Hermitian systems as degeneracies, where not only eigenvalues but also eigenvectors coalesce. They are of great theoretical and experimental interest due to their exotic topological properties and enhanced sensitivity to perturbations. Experimental realizations of higher-order exceptional points, where more than two eigenvectors coalesce, rely on highly fine-tuned setups. Recently, stimulated Brillouin scattering has been employed to generate second-order exceptional points in a fabrication-free setup by leveraging off-resonant scattering. In this work we generalize this approach, and we develop an off-resonant, multimode theory for stimulated Brillouin scattering as an avenue towards realizing symmetry-induced exceptional points of any order. We present the experimental implementation of our program in an accompanying paper. Our multimode theory could also be employed in applications in optoacoustic sensing, synthetic neuromorphic computing, microwave photonic filters, and optoacoustic quantum signal processing.
tldr: This paper develops a multimode theory for stimulated Brillouin scattering to realize higher-order exceptional points in a continuum optoacoustic system.
motivation: Higher-order exceptional points are of interest for their topological properties and enhanced sensitivity, but experimental realizations require fine-tuning. The authors aim to generalize a previous approach using stimulated Brillouin scattering to achieve symmetry-induced exceptional points of any order in a fabrication-free setup.
method: The authors develop an off-resonant, multimode theory for stimulated Brillouin scattering, leveraging the continuum of optical and acoustic modes to create degeneracies where multiple eigenvectors coalesce.
result: The theory predicts the possibility of realizing exceptional points of any order in a multimode optoacoustic system, with an accompanying experimental implementation reported separately.
conclusion: The work opens avenues for applications in optoacoustic sensing, neuromorphic computing, microwave photonic filters, and quantum signal processing, though the direct relevance to the user's research interests is limited.

title: Hydrodynamics Of The Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou Chain
authors: Abhishek Dhar Shubhadeep Chakraborty
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a pedagogical review of the hydrodynamics of the FPUT chain. There are three hydrodynamic fields corresponding to the conservation of mass, momentum and energy. We provide physically motivated derivations of the hydrodynamic equations at the levels of Euler and then Navier-Stokes-Fourier. Next we consider examples to test as to how successful the hydrodynamic description is in predicting the observed time evolution of nonequilibrium initial conditions such as domain walls and blasts. We find that in some cases there is good agreement of microscopic simulations with predictions from the Euler equations while, in several other cases, there is significant departure from the Euler predictions suggesting that the role of dissipation and noise is important in general.
tldr: This paper reviews the hydrodynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chain, deriving Euler and Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations and testing them against microscopic simulations.
motivation: To understand the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions for nonlinear lattice systems, particularly for nonequilibrium initial conditions.
method: Pedagogical derivation of hydrodynamic equations from conservation laws, followed by comparison of Euler and Navier-Stokes-Fourier predictions with molecular dynamics simulations.
result: Euler equations agree well with simulations for some initial conditions (e.g., domain walls) but fail for others (e.g., blasts), indicating the importance of dissipation and noise.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic theory is partially successful for the FPUT chain, but further work is needed to incorporate dissipation and noise for a complete description.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Nonlinear PDEs: When And Where Hybridization Is Effective?
authors: Kaveh Zabihi, Hamid Montazeri, Akke S. J. Suiker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle on nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) with sharp gradients, stiff dynamics, high-frequency content, or multiscale structure. Such limitations, rooted in spectral bias, ill-conditioned optimization, and unstable convergence, restrict PINN accuracy in regimes where advanced solvers are most needed. In this work, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural network (HQPINN) that integrates a classical neural-network backbone with a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) to enrich the solution representation. The framework is benchmarked against a classical PINN on three representative nonlinear PDEs: Burgers' equation, the Allen-Cahn equation, and the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. The framework is further examined through a systematic sensitivity analysis of qubit count, circuit depth, PQC placement, collocation density, and classical-network width. Across all benchmarks, HQPINNs exhibit smoother training dynamics, reduced loss oscillations, and improved final accuracy, with the largest gains occurring in stiff and multiscale regimes. Relative L2 error decreases by about fourfold for Burgers' equation and fivefold for the Allen-Cahn equation, while improvements for the KdV equation are more moderate. Overall, the results demonstrate that carefully co-designed hybrid quantum-classical architectures can mitigate key limitations of classical PINNs and provide practical design guidance for near-term quantum-enhanced PDE solvers.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical PINN for solving nonlinear PDEs, showing improved accuracy in stiff and multiscale regimes.
motivation: Classical PINNs struggle with nonlinear PDEs due to spectral bias and ill-conditioned optimization; the authors aim to mitigate these issues by integrating quantum circuits.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural network (HQPINN) is developed, combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit, and benchmarked on Burgers', Allen-Cahn, and KdV equations.
result: HQPINNs achieve smoother training, reduced loss oscillations, and up to fivefold reduction in relative L2 error compared to classical PINNs, especially in stiff and multiscale regimes.
conclusion: Carefully co-designed hybrid architectures can mitigate limitations of classical PINNs, providing guidance for near-term quantum-enhanced PDE solvers.

title: Digital Quantum Reservoir Computing For Atm Time Series Prediction
authors: Chiara Vercellino, Giacomo Vitali, Valeria Zaffaroni, Francesca Cibrario, Emanuele Dri, Paolo Viviani, Olivier Terzo, Davide Corbelletto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a digital quantum reservoir computing (QRC) framework for multi-step forecasting of automated teller machine (ATM) cash demand time series on near-term quantum devices. The proposed approach uses parametrized four-qubit reservoirs with a fixed structure exploiting partial measurement and reset, where temporal data is encoded in rotation angles. Training is restricted to a classical Ridge-regression readout. We systematically analyze the impact of the circuit ansatz\"e, reservoir memory, measurement-derived observables, and the execution backend on the forecasting performance. Experiments are performed with noiseless simulation, noise-aware emulation, and a real IQM Spark quantum processor. Although the QRC models do not outperform the classical Prophet benchmark in terms of Mean Absolute Error and Normalized Mean Squared Error metrics, they achieve more competitive results in Dynamic Time Warping metric, indicating a partial ability to capture temporal structure. These findings provide an empirical assessment of digital QRC for realistic financial forecasting and highlight both its current limitations and its potential on near-term quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper applies digital quantum reservoir computing to ATM cash demand forecasting, finding that QRC does not outperform classical methods but shows some ability to capture temporal structure.
motivation: To explore the practical utility of near-term quantum devices for financial time series forecasting, specifically ATM cash demand prediction.
method: A four-qubit parametrized quantum circuit reservoir with partial measurement and reset is used; temporal data is encoded via rotation angles, and training is done with classical ridge regression. Experiments include noiseless simulation, noise-aware emulation, and real quantum processor execution.
result: QRC models do not beat the classical Prophet benchmark in MAE and NMSE, but achieve competitive Dynamic Time Warping scores, indicating partial temporal structure capture.
conclusion: Digital QRC shows potential for financial forecasting but currently underperforms classical methods; further improvements in hardware and reservoir design are needed.

title: The Coercivity Gap In Neural Pde Solvers: Parameter Escape And Functional Convergence
authors: Enrique Zuazua
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study neural approximation of elliptic PDE solutions from a variational perspective. The central point is the distinction between the geometry of neural parameters and the convergence of the corresponding physical states. Even when the original elliptic energy is coercive and strictly convex in the natural energy space, its restriction to a nonlinear neural ansatz may fail to be coercive in parameter space. This failure is caused by non-closedness of neural approximation manifolds and by condensation of neurons, which may generate limiting profiles outside the fixed ansatz class. Nevertheless, the associated state functions may remain bounded and converge strongly to the exact PDE solution. We prove this mechanism for Gaussian wave-packet approximations of a prototypical elliptic model in the whole space, derive convergence rates, and explain how the same state-level stability principle applies to residual minimization methods of PINN type, and HYCO-type hybrid methods. We also discuss relaxation and Tikhonov regularization.
tldr: This paper studies neural approximation of elliptic PDE solutions, focusing on the coercivity gap in parameter space due to non-closedness of neural manifolds and neuron condensation.
motivation: To understand why neural network approximations of PDE solutions can converge in state space even when the parameter optimization problem is ill-posed (non-coercive).
method: Theoretical analysis using variational principles, Gaussian wave-packet approximations, and residual minimization methods (PINN, HYCO).
result: Proves that state-level convergence can occur despite parameter-level non-coercivity, and derives convergence rates for a prototypical elliptic model.
conclusion: The findings explain stability of neural PDE solvers and suggest relaxation/Tikhonov regularization to mitigate parameter escape.

title: Nonlocal Mean Field Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge With Learned Interactions
authors: Daisuke Inoue, Mathieu Lauri\`ere, Dante Kalise
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schr\"odinger Bridge Problem constructs a stochastic process that connects an initial distribution to a terminal distribution with minimum energy. This work considers its mean-field extension, the Mean-Field Schr\"odinger Bridge, for interacting particle systems. With nonlocal interactions, evaluating the resulting particle-dependent distributional terms can scale quadratically with the population size, which makes large-scale problems intractable. We address this bottleneck by approximating the nonlocal interactions with neural network surrogates. The resulting four-stage alternating algorithm reduces the per-step cost from quadratic to linear in the population size at inference. We also derive Gr\"onwall-type stability bounds that show how surrogate errors propagate to the generated trajectories. In numerical experiments on navigation and opinion-dynamics tasks, the proposed method reproduces trajectories obtained with analytical evaluation and reduces training time.
tldr: This paper proposes a neural network surrogate to reduce computational cost of nonlocal interactions in mean-field Schrödinger bridge problems.
motivation: Evaluating nonlocal interactions in mean-field Schrödinger bridge scales quadratically with population size, making large-scale problems intractable.
method: The authors approximate nonlocal interactions with neural network surrogates and develop a four-stage alternating algorithm that reduces per-step cost from quadratic to linear in population size at inference.
result: The method reproduces trajectories obtained with analytical evaluation and reduces training time in navigation and opinion-dynamics tasks.
conclusion: The approach enables scalable mean-field Schrödinger bridge for interacting particle systems, with potential applications in multi-agent systems and collective behavior.

title: Local Sensitivity Under Transport Restrictions
authors: Hongseok Namkoong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We quantify the value of structural knowledge, restrictions a modeler places on the world before seeing data. Our analytic workhorse is the local sensitivity of an estimand to distributional perturbations in the Otto-Wasserstein geometry: the largest first-order change in the estimand per unit displacement of probability mass (transport), equal to the dual norm of the spatial gradient of the efficient influence function. The modeler encodes structural knowledge by restricting the class of transports, and the resulting reduction in sensitivity is the value of their inductive bias. We illustrate by shedding light on a longstanding puzzle in causal inference where classical semiparametric efficiency bounds remain identical regardless of whether the propensity score is known, despite observed practical difficulties when it is unknown. Our approach characterizes how known propensities significantly reduce sensitivity to misspecification.
tldr: This paper quantifies the value of structural knowledge in statistical modeling using local sensitivity under Wasserstein transport restrictions, with an application to causal inference.
motivation: To formalize how prior structural knowledge (inductive bias) reduces sensitivity to model misspecification, particularly in causal inference where known propensity scores do not improve semiparametric efficiency bounds but reduce sensitivity.
method: The authors define local sensitivity as the largest first-order change in an estimand per unit displacement of probability mass in the Otto-Wasserstein geometry, and restrict the class of transports to encode structural knowledge.
result: The reduction in sensitivity due to transport restrictions quantifies the value of inductive bias; the approach explains why known propensity scores reduce sensitivity to misspecification despite unchanged efficiency bounds.
conclusion: The framework provides a new way to measure the value of structural assumptions, with implications for robust inference and model selection.

title: The Preisach Extremum Stack Is A Shannon-Minimal Sufficient Statistic For Rate-Independent Functionals
authors: Piotr Frydrych
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let R denote the class of all computable, causal functionals that are rate-independent in the classical sense (invariant under monotone time reparametrizations), and let Pi_n be the Preisach extremum stack of an input sequence u_{0:n}. We prove a characterization theorem establishing that every F in R satisfies Fu = f(Pi_n) for a computable f, and derive two information-theoretic results. First, under any probability measure on u_{0:n}, the equality I(u_{0:n}; Fu) = I(Pi_n; Fu) holds for every F in R and is an immediate corollary of the characterization theorem. Second, the main result: Pi_n is a Shannon-minimal sufficient statistic in the sense that I(u_{0:n}; Pi_n) <= I(u_{0:n}; S) for every random variable S from which all R-queries are computable. The proof uses the finite indicator family of [Frydrych, 2026] to reconstruct Pi_n from any sufficient S. As a corollary, online maintenance of Pi_n suffices for rate-independent estimation: the NNLS estimator of the Preisach measure mu can be assembled from the incremental stack process (Pi_t)_{t=0}^n in O(k * L^2) memory per step, where k = |Pi_t| and L is the grid resolution.
tldr: The paper proves that the Preisach extremum stack is a Shannon-minimal sufficient statistic for rate-independent functionals, with implications for efficient estimation of the Preisach measure.
motivation: To characterize the class of rate-independent functionals and identify a minimal sufficient statistic that captures all information needed for such functionals.
method: The author uses a characterization theorem to show that every rate-independent functional can be expressed as a function of the Preisach extremum stack, and then applies information-theoretic arguments to prove minimal sufficiency.
result: The Preisach extremum stack is a Shannon-minimal sufficient statistic for rate-independent functionals, and online maintenance of the stack suffices for rate-independent estimation with low memory cost.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for efficient computation in rate-independent systems, with potential applications in hysteresis modeling and signal processing.

title: Hardness As An Information Constraint: A Unifying Meta-Complexity Assumption
authors: Hunter Monroe
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monroe (2026) shows that the nonexistence of an optimal proof system can be read as an information constraint regarding canonical hard instances: no sound arithmetic theory simulates the extensions adjoining sufficiently large, unprovable Busy Beaver values. Furthermore, if the best-known route to simulation is also necessary -- that is, if simulation requires a relative-consistency explanation over a weak base theory -- then the same constraint holds for inaccessible Kolmogorov-randomness facts. Call this Kolmogorov Hardness (KH). We argue that open questions in computational complexity can likewise be reformulated as information constraints involving Kolmogorov-random strings. Variants of KH yield, as conditional consequences, dense families of small hard tautologies, no-mutual-help phenomena for independent random axioms, PH noncollapse with explicit dense separators at each level, [MATH], and canonical disjoint NP pairs arising from random-axiom constructions. Time-bounded and sparse-support variants extend the same template to one-way functions via Liu--Pass, derandomization, natural-proofs-style limitations, and Feige-style random refutation. This framework gives a unified working model of complexity theorists' beliefs, organized around canonical hard instances. It seems self-evident that efficient proofs in a theory should not leverage true randomness facts the theory cannot verify. Yet the structural features of KH and its variants suggest they may be formally independent of standard metatheories. They behave like reflection principles; their internal readings fail in nonstandard models even when the corresponding external readings are true; and the same information constraints may apply to the metatheories themselves. We propose a research program: extend the model, resolve questions of formal independence, and identify which principles are potential new axioms.
tldr: This paper proposes a meta-complexity assumption called Kolmogorov Hardness (KH) that unifies various open problems in computational complexity as information constraints involving Kolmogorov-random strings.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for understanding hardness in computational complexity through the lens of information constraints, and to explore the formal independence of such principles.
method: The paper builds on prior work by Monroe (2026) and extends the concept of information constraints to Kolmogorov-random strings, defining KH and its variants, and deriving conditional consequences for complexity theory.
result: KH yields conditional results such as dense families of small hard tautologies, no-mutual-help phenomena, PH noncollapse, and connections to one-way functions, derandomization, and natural proofs.
conclusion: KH behaves like reflection principles and may be formally independent of standard metatheories; the paper proposes a research program to extend the model and resolve questions of formal independence.

title: What Can Verifiable Decapsulation Tests Certify? Pass Bounds And Fault-Recognition Limits For FO-Based KEMs
authors: Jos\'e Luis Delgado Jim\'enez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black-box tests for Fujisaki-Okamoto decapsulation observe the sampled execution seen by the harness, whereas the reencryption computation itself is visible only through the values that reach final key derivation. We study confirmation-code-augmented KEM variants under an honest-reference harness in which the reference encapsulation fixes a hidden final-key point [MATH], with [MATH] the confirmation witness. For a [MATH]-localized system under test, acceptance is bounded by honest correctness error, adversarial aliasing, final-key freshness defects, a hit on the localized suffix list [MATH], and [MATH]. A one-query construction from any predictor of [MATH] matches this bound up to the fresh-key coincidence term, so the list-hit event is the black-box obstruction measured by the harness. The list-hit term is bounded either by a cUP-faithful harness certificate, which transfers source confirmation-code unpredictability with a [MATH]-loss, or by an average conditional min-entropy bound, with separate RawEnt and TailEnt hypotheses for short diagnostic and truncation-tail codes. The same model proves a dependency-cone lower bound for non-certification claims. When the black-box observation of an honest-support harness factors through the confirmation-observable final-key target, every operation outside the support-active cone has a coupled erasure implementation with the same transcript distribution; over any implementation class containing that erasure, soundness and completeness errors of an execution certifier satisfy [MATH]. The ML-KEM and HQC case studies distinguish theorem-covered positive rows, finite-catalog artifact rows, and non-certification rows that carry a cone-inactivity certificate. The security of the standard KEM lines is the construction-level security supplied by the cited source analyses.
tldr: This paper analyzes security bounds and fault-recognition limits for Fujisaki-Okamoto-based key encapsulation mechanisms using verifiable decapsulation tests, focusing on black-box observation and confirmation codes.
motivation: To understand what can be certified by verifiable decapsulation tests in FO-based KEMs, particularly regarding security guarantees and limitations under adversarial conditions.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model with an honest-reference harness, confirmation-code-augmented KEM variants, and analyze acceptance bounds using concepts like list-hit events, min-entropy bounds, and dependency cones.
result: Acceptance is bounded by several factors including honest correctness error, adversarial aliasing, and a list-hit term; a one-query construction matches this bound; a dependency-cone lower bound for non-certification claims is proven.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for certifying FO-based KEMs, with case studies on ML-KEM and HQC, but the results are highly specialized to post-quantum cryptography and not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Near-Perfect Chirality And Giant Spin-Orbit Conversion In A Single Plasmonic Cavity
authors: Lin Ma, Zhong-Jian Yang, Xiao-Jing Du, Yue You, Kun Zhang, Jun He, Jianfang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To overcome the difficulty of single nanostructures in approaching the theoretical limit of chiroptical performance, we design a single plasmonic twisted dimer cavity whose magnetic gap plasmon mode enables magnetic polarization near-field engineering for high chirality. The structure exhibits strong extinction under circularly polarized excitation with one handedness, while its response to the orthogonally circularly polarized light is almost perfectly suppressed, yielding a chiral g-factor as high as 1.94. Meanwhile, the structure demonstrates strong chiral-selective spin-orbit angular momentum conversion: the conversion efficiency is ~95% under circularly polarized excitation with one handedness and only ~1% under the other. By tuning geometric parameters, the g-factor can be continuously adjusted from 0 to 1.94. Without relying on periodic coupling or collective effects, this work achieves near-perfect chirality and highly efficient angular momentum manipulation solely through intrinsic near-field matching, providing a new design strategy and theoretical basis for highly selective, ultra-compact integrated chiral photonic devices.
tldr: A single plasmonic twisted dimer cavity achieves near-perfect chirality and giant spin-orbit conversion via magnetic gap plasmon mode engineering.
motivation: To overcome the difficulty of single nanostructures in approaching the theoretical limit of chiroptical performance.
method: Design of a single plasmonic twisted dimer cavity that uses magnetic gap plasmon mode for magnetic polarization near-field engineering.
result: Chiral g-factor up to 1.94, spin-orbit conversion efficiency ~95% for one handedness and ~1% for the other, tunable g-factor from 0 to 1.94.
conclusion: Provides a new design strategy for ultra-compact integrated chiral photonic devices without relying on periodic coupling or collective effects.

title: Functional Interface Blocks For Neuromorphic Hardware: A Junction-Centered Framework
authors: Wellington Avelino, Yann Beillard, Fabien Allibart, Dominique Drouin, Gilberto Medeiros-Ribeiro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterogeneous neuromorphic hardware integrates devices with dissimilar electrical characteristics and dynamics, making functional compatibility at their interconnections a primary design challenge. Direct coupling alone is insufficient to ensure correct operation, because the load-line conditions established at each junction determine the effective operating regime. Here, we propose a junction-centered interface framework in which inter-device connections are described through assigned drive/sense roles and organized into canonical functional interface blocks. As a concrete hardware realization, a second-generation current conveyor (CCII)-based implementation is then adopted as a composite realization of these interface primitives. The framework is validated experimentally in a Pavlovian-conditioning demonstrator combining a memristive synapse with a unijunction-transistor (UJT) post-neuron. By linking local junction conditions to reusable interface functions, the proposed methodology provides a systematic basis for the design and analysis of heterogeneous neuromorphic systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a junction-centered interface framework for heterogeneous neuromorphic hardware, using a current conveyor implementation to ensure functional compatibility between devices.
motivation: Heterogeneous neuromorphic hardware faces challenges in functional compatibility at interconnections due to dissimilar device characteristics; direct coupling is insufficient.
method: The authors define drive/sense roles for inter-device connections and organize them into canonical functional interface blocks, realized via a second-generation current conveyor (CCII) circuit.
result: The framework is validated experimentally in a Pavlovian-conditioning demonstrator combining a memristive synapse with a unijunction-transistor post-neuron.
conclusion: The methodology provides a systematic basis for designing and analyzing heterogeneous neuromorphic systems, linking local junction conditions to reusable interface functions.

title: Delta-pulse Solution In Zener Viscoelastic Model
authors: Andrea Mentrelli, Juan Luis Gonzalez-Santander, Francesco Mainardi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the integral representation of the solution for the propagation of a delta-pulse (impulsive wave) in a semi-infinite, homogeneous, linear viscoelastic medium governed by the Zener model. Starting from the Bromwich integral representation of the response function, we obtain a closed-form integral representation by analytically inverting the relevant Laplace transforms. The result is expressed in terms of modified Bessel functions of the first kind and Macdonald functions of half-integer order, and is shown to reduce to the known Maxwell model solution in the appropriate limit. As an independent computational approach, we derive the steepest descent path (SDP) associated with the phase function of the Bromwich integral, characterizing its saddle points and showing that the SDP can be expressed explicitly as the zero locus of a sixth-degree polynomial in the imaginary part of the complex variable. The two methods are compared numerically for several values of the model parameters, confirming their agreement. While the integral representation provides analytical insight into the structure of the solution, the steepest descent method requires no explicit inversion of the Laplace transform and may therefore prove especially valuable in more general viscoelastic settings where a closed-form integral representation is not available.
tldr: This paper derives an integral representation for the propagation of a delta-pulse in a Zener viscoelastic medium using Laplace transform inversion and steepest descent methods.
motivation: To obtain an analytical solution for impulsive wave propagation in a Zener viscoelastic model, which is a classic problem in viscoelasticity.
method: The authors start from the Bromwich integral representation of the response function, analytically invert Laplace transforms to obtain a closed-form integral representation in terms of modified Bessel and Macdonald functions, and also derive the steepest descent path for numerical evaluation.
result: The solution is expressed in terms of modified Bessel functions of the first kind and Macdonald functions of half-integer order, and reduces to the Maxwell model solution in the appropriate limit. The steepest descent method agrees numerically with the integral representation.
conclusion: The integral representation provides analytical insight, while the steepest descent method offers a computational approach that may be valuable for more general viscoelastic models where closed-form solutions are unavailable.

title: Highly Efficient Difference-frequency Generation For Mid-infrared Pulses By Passively Synchronous Seeding
authors: Kun Huang, Yinqi Wang, Jianan Fang, Huaixi Chen, Minghang Xu, Qiang Hao, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have proposed and experimentally demonstrated a novel scheme for efficient mid-infrared difference-frequency generation based on passively synchronized fiber lasers. The adoption of coincident seeding pulses in the nonlinear conversion process could substantially lower the pumping threshold for mid-infrared parametric emission. Consequently, a picosecond mid-infrared source at 3.1 [MATH]m was prepared with watt-level average power, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of 77\% was realized from pump to down-converted light. Additionally, the long-term stability of generated power was manifested with a relative fluctuation as low as 0.17\% over one hour. Thanks to the all-optical passive synchronization and all-polarization-maintaining fiber architecture, the implemented laser system was also featured with simplicity, compactness and robustness, which would favor subsequent applications beyond laboratory operation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a highly efficient mid-infrared difference-frequency generation scheme using passively synchronized fiber lasers, achieving 77% power conversion efficiency and excellent stability.
motivation: To develop a simple, compact, and robust mid-infrared laser source with high efficiency and stability for applications beyond laboratory settings.
method: Passively synchronized fiber lasers provide coincident seeding pulses for difference-frequency generation in a nonlinear crystal, lowering the pumping threshold.
result: A picosecond mid-infrared source at 3.1 μm with watt-level average power, 77% conversion efficiency, and 0.17% power fluctuation over one hour was achieved.
conclusion: The all-optical passive synchronization and all-polarization-maintaining fiber architecture yield a practical, robust laser system suitable for real-world applications.

title: Coincidence-pumping Upconversion Detector Based On Passively Synchronized Fiber Laser System
authors: Weiyan Kang, Bowen Li, Yan Liang, Qiang Hao, Ming Yan, Kun Huang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a high-performance frequency upconversion detector for telecom-band photons based on a passively synchronized fiber laser system. The involved coincidence pumping technique enabled to spectrally convert the pulsed infrared photons into the visible regime with a conversion efficiency of 72\%. The overall detection efficiency of the upconversion detector reached to 30\% with a low noise equivalent power of [MATH]. In contrast to previous demonstrations, the whole upconversion detection system was constructed in an all-polarization-maintaining fiber structure, thus favoring substantial improvement of compactness and robustness. title: Reconstructing Unobservable Temperature Fields Via Simulation-Aided Intelligent Sensing
authors: Monika Stipsitz, H\`elios Sanchis-Alepuz, Jacob Reynvaan, Silvester Sabathiel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time monitoring of the temperature distribution within components and sub-structures is a challenging topic in many systems due to restrictions on feasible sensor locations. While machine learning (ML) proves a versatile tool in many applications, its adoption for high-resolution thermal monitoring is hindered by the availability of high-quality datasets for training. In this work, we propose a novel approach for generating datasets for industrial applications based on randomized physics-based simulations. We demonstrate the approach in a proof-of-concept hardware setup: A neural network (NN) trained only on such a synthetic dataset, is used to reconstruct the internal temperature field from sparse sensors embedded in the hardware. The NN-based reconstructions do not only outperform Kriging in robustness but also enable real-time inference, making the method suitable for online monitoring of otherwise unobservable thermal states.
tldr: This paper uses physics-based simulations to generate synthetic datasets for training a neural network to reconstruct unobservable temperature fields from sparse sensors.
motivation: Real-time monitoring of temperature distributions is challenging due to restricted sensor locations and lack of high-quality training data.
method: Randomized physics-based simulations generate synthetic datasets; a neural network is trained on this synthetic data to reconstruct internal temperature fields from sparse sensor measurements.
result: The neural network outperforms Kriging in robustness and enables real-time inference, making it suitable for online monitoring.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates that synthetic data from simulations can effectively train ML models for thermal monitoring, with potential for industrial applications.

title: On The Conicality Of Causally Simple, Future Cohesive Spacetimes

title: Semantic Constraint Synthesis For Adaptive Trajectory Optimization Via Large Language Models
authors: Eleanor Brosius, Yuji Takubo, Daniele Gammelli, Simone D'amico, Marco Pavone
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trajectory optimization is a critical component for enabling safe and reliable autonomous operations in space exploration. As space missions increase in frequency, complexity, and scope, there is a growing need to rapidly formulate mathematically sound trajectory optimization problems that accurately reflect mission objectives and operational constraints. However, translating mission intent into tractable analytical formulations for trajectory optimization requires substantial domain expertise. This paper presents a framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to translate natural language descriptions of mission requirements and constraints into executable trajectory optimization code and corresponding mathematical formulations. Experiments in spacecraft rendezvous scenarios demonstrate a high success rate in reconditioning a convex trajectory optimization problem from semantic mission requirements. Ultimately, this work highlights the potential of LLMs to bridge high-level intent and formal optimization models, enabling more flexible and efficient trajectory design of spacecraft.
tldr: This paper uses large language models to translate natural language mission requirements into trajectory optimization code for spacecraft rendezvous.
motivation: To reduce the domain expertise needed to formulate trajectory optimization problems for space missions.
method: A framework that leverages LLMs to convert natural language descriptions into executable optimization code and mathematical formulations.
result: High success rate in reconditioning convex trajectory optimization problems from semantic mission requirements.
conclusion: LLMs can bridge high-level intent and formal optimization models, enabling more flexible trajectory design.

title: An Energy-Stable Implicit Convex-Splitting Bdf2 Scheme For The Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: Qi Wang Xuelong Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an energy-stable implicit convex-splitting BDF2 discretization (CS-BDF2) of the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes equations. For the Cahn--Hilliard equation, BDF2 analyses can establish energy stability by testing the phase equation in the (H^{-1}) metric. For CHNS, this test is not compatible with the coupled energy estimate: the momentum equation is tested by (\bfu^{n+1}), while the transported phase equation is tested by (\mu^{n+1}) so that transport cancels capillary work. The chemical-potential relation must then be paired with the BDF2 phase increment ((3\phi^{n+1}-4\phi^n+\phi^{n-1})/2); its nonlinear part must produce a BDF2 bulk-energy difference, up to nonnegative higher-order history terms. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a new BDF2-compatible convex-splitting approximation of the nonlinear bulk force that directly yields a discrete bulk-energy identity and enables a discrete energy analysis for the CHNS system. conclusion: The proposed CS-BDF2 scheme provides a robust numerical method for simulating phase-field fluid dynamics, with potential extensions to other complex fluid systems.

title: Unbiased Estimation Of Squared Concentration In The Fisher-von Mises-Langevin Distribution And The Impossibility Of Unbiased Concentration

abstract: ArXiv:2606.04267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The estimation of concentration parameter in Fisher-von Mises-Langevin distribution is the directional statistics analogue of the estimation of the precision matrix for the Gaussian distribution. title: Exponential Time Differencing Schemes For A Phase-Field Model Of Multicomponent Membranes
authors: Wangbo Luo, Zhonghua Qiao, Yanxiang Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze exponential time differencing (ETD) schemes for a phase-field model of multicomponent membranes proposed in our previous work , in which membrane deformation is governed by a force-balance phase-field equation and protein segregation is described by a membrane-associated Ohta-Kawasaki (OK) dynamics. title: A Novel Class Of High-order Uniformly Accurate Exponential Integrators With Local Linear Extension For The Charged-particle Dynamics Under Strong Magnetic Field

title: Numerical Analysis Of The Second-order Time-dependent Saddle Point Maxwell System Via A Parameter-free Discontinuous Galerkin Method: The First Optimal ${\bf L}^{2}$-norm Error Estimates

title: Enhanced Fluid Index Modulation For Integrated Data And Energy Transfer
authors: Long Zhang, Yizhe Zhao, Halvin Yang, Qiang Liu, Kai-Kit Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated data and energy transfer (IDET) is a promising technique for supporting sustainable low-power wireless networks. To improve both communication reliability and energy transfer efficiency, this paper investigates a fluid index modulation (FIM) assisted IDET system, where the base station employs a two-dimensional fluid antenna system (FAS) and the receiver adopts a power-splitting architecture. In FIM, the information bits are delivered not only from the modulation symbols, but also the index of antenna position. Under finite-alphabet signaling, the average harvested power, bit error rate (BER), and achievable data rate are derived in closed form. A joint optimization problem is formulated to maximize the average harvested power subject to BER and achievable rate constraints by jointly optimizing the port selection, precoding vector, and power splitting ratio. An alternating optimization framework is developed, where the precoding vector and port selection are obtained via a Riemannian augmented Lagrangian method (RALM) and block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a superior rate-energy trade-off over benchmark schemes, while the proposed algorithm attains near-optimal performance with significantly lower complexity than exhaustive search.

motivation: To support sustainable low-power wireless networks by enhancing both data transmission and energy harvesting simultaneously.

conclusion: FIM-IDET is a promising approach for future wireless networks, but the paper focuses on classical communication and energy transfer, with no quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

tldr: This paper refines a technical estimate in Chen's reverse-heat coupling approach to Talagrand's convolution conjecture on the Boolean cube, achieving a logarithmic improvement.
motivation: To improve upon Chen's result regarding the terminal testing-discrepancy in the context of Talagrand's convolution conjecture on the Boolean cube.
method: The authors use a joint-filtration martingale formulation of Chen's coupling and exploit approximate monotonicity and conditional squared-score estimates to prove a localized testing estimate.
result: They prove a localized terminal testing discrepancy bound that yields a logarithmic improvement over Chen's result for the Boolean heat semigroup.
conclusion: The work provides a refined estimate that advances the understanding of Talagrand's convolution conjecture, but its direct applicability to the user's research interests is limited.

title: Lipschitz Stable Sequence Classes: An Approach To Rademacher Type And Cotype Of Lipschitz Functions
authors: D. Ruiz-Casternado
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we extend sequence-class methods from linear and multilinear theory to the Lipschitz setting, highlighting the substantial differences that arise from the lack of linearity. First, we establish a general criterion for lifting a Lipschitz mapping between Banach spaces to a Lipschitz operator between sequence spaces, and we use it to define the class [MATH] of [MATH]-summing Lipschitz functions, where [MATH] and [MATH] are sequence classes. We then introduce the notion of Lipschitz stable sequence class and show that [MATH] is a Banach Lipschitz ideal whenever the sequence classes satisfy this property. As applications, we present Rademacher type and cotype for Lipschitz functions and identify them with [MATH]-summing Lipschitz spaces for concrete choices of sequence classes. We prove that the type case forms a Banach Lipschitz ideal, whereas the cotype case does not, and we analyse composition and maximality for the type ideals.
tldr: This paper extends sequence-class methods to Lipschitz functions, defining summing Lipschitz ideals and analyzing Rademacher type and cotype in the Lipschitz setting.
motivation: To generalize linear and multilinear sequence-class methods to the nonlinear Lipschitz setting, addressing challenges due to lack of linearity.
method: Introduces Lipschitz stable sequence classes and uses them to define Banach Lipschitz ideals of summing Lipschitz functions; applies to Rademacher type and cotype.
result: Establishes that type forms a Banach Lipschitz ideal while cotype does not, and analyzes composition and maximality for type ideals.
conclusion: Provides a framework for Lipschitz analogues of classical sequence-class concepts, with implications for nonlinear functional analysis.

title: Optimal Control Of Sweeping Processes With Nonsmooth Moving Sets: A Numerical Algorithm
authors: Chadi Nour
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper extends the numerical method introduced by de Pinho et al. [22] and later developed in Nour and Zeidan [33, 37] to the nonautonomous case where the nonsmooth sweeping set depends explicitly on time. The moving character of the sweeping set creates substantial additional difficulties, since several geometric constants involved in the analysis may a priori depend on time. To overcome this issue, we establish uniform geometric estimates for the moving constraint sets and their boundaries. These estimates allow us to extend the discrete approximation scheme developed in [22, 33, 37] and prove its convergence toward admissible solutions of the original problem. Several examples illustrating the applicability of the proposed method are also presented.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical algorithm for optimal control of sweeping processes with nonsmooth moving sets, focusing on mathematical convergence proofs.
motivation: To extend existing numerical methods for sweeping processes to the nonautonomous case where the constraint set moves in time, which introduces additional geometric difficulties.
method: The authors establish uniform geometric estimates for moving constraint sets and their boundaries, then extend a discrete approximation scheme and prove its convergence.
result: The proposed algorithm converges to admissible solutions of the original optimal control problem, demonstrated with examples.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous numerical framework for optimal control with time-dependent nonsmooth constraints, with potential applications in mechanics and engineering.

title: Well-posedness And Finite Element Approximation Of The Electrostatic Shear Alfv\'en Wave Equations
authors: Annalisa Buffa, Timon Miehling, Marco Picasso, Markus Renoldner
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the well-posedness and finite element approximation of the electrostatic shear Alfv\'en wave equations, a coupled system of two partial differential equations arising in plasma physics as a simplified sub-model of the drift-reduced Braginskii equations. To this end, anisotropic Sobolev spaces depending on the normalized magnetic field [MATH] are introduced, together with a Poincar\'e-type inequality along the integral curves of [MATH], which holds under a geometric directedness condition on the magnetic field. Using these tools, existence, uniqueness, and stability of a weak solution are established via the Faedo-Galerkin method. It is also shown that the geometric condition is satisfied in tokamak and stellarator configurations. A numerical scheme is then proposed, combining Lagrange finite elements in space with a Crank-Nicolson discretization in time. The scheme is shown to conserve a discrete energy exactly in the homogeneous case, and a priori error estimates are derived in the natural energy norm. Several numerical experiments are reported in two and three space dimensions, which confirm the theoretical results and indicate that the geometric condition on the magnetic field is necessary for the invertibility of the discrete system matrix.
tldr: This paper studies the well-posedness and finite element approximation of electrostatic shear Alfvén wave equations in plasma physics, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a rigorous mathematical analysis and numerical scheme for a simplified plasma model, ensuring existence, uniqueness, and stability of solutions.
method: Introduces anisotropic Sobolev spaces and a Poincaré-type inequality, uses Faedo-Galerkin method for well-posedness, and proposes a finite element scheme with Crank-Nicolson time discretization.
result: Establishes well-posedness under a geometric condition on the magnetic field, proves discrete energy conservation, and derives a priori error estimates; numerical experiments confirm theory.
conclusion: The geometric condition is necessary for invertibility of the discrete system, and the method is applicable to tokamak and stellarator configurations.

title: Local-global Conjugacy Questions For Affine Extensions
authors: Dean Wardell
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boston and Jones constructed a probabilistic model, called the Markov model, in order to predict the cycle structures of elements in Galois groups [MATH] associated to the [MATH]-th iterate of a quadratic postcritically finite polynomial [MATH] over a number field. Goksel refined this model, introducing the 'even' Markov groups [MATH]. These groups conjecturally contain a copy of [MATH], leading to questions about local-global conjugacies within the larger automorphism group [MATH] of the first [MATH] levels of the binary rooted tree coming from arboreal representations of the Galois groups. While the conjugacy results found by Goksel were restricted to the study of these automorphism groups, we generalise the findings to affine extensions of groups by permutation representations, using a cohomological argument. Furthermore, we provide a counterexample to the main conjecture proposed by Goksel, demonstrating that more work is required to resolve the underlying questions regarding Markov models.
tldr: This paper studies local-global conjugacy in affine extensions of automorphism groups of binary rooted trees, related to Galois groups of iterated quadratic polynomials, and provides a counterexample to a conjecture by Goksel.
motivation: To understand the structure of Galois groups arising from iterated quadratic polynomials and to test conjectures about Markov models predicting cycle structures.
method: Cohomological arguments and group-theoretic analysis of affine extensions by permutation representations.
result: Generalized Goksel's conjugacy results to affine extensions and found a counterexample to Goksel's main conjecture.
conclusion: More work is needed to resolve questions about Markov models; the counterexample shows the conjecture is false.

title: Fitting Scattered Data With Optional Monotonicity Constraints On Gpu: LipFit Package
authors: Gleb Beliakov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a method of multivariate scattered data interpolation and approximation that produces optimal Lipschitz-continuous approximation, subject to the desired monotonicity constraints. This method relies on tight upper and lower approximations to the data, and is similar in its spirit to the nearest-neighbour approximation but does not suffer from discontinuities. Local Lipschitz interpolation and Lipschitz smoothing are also presented. This approach falls under the umbrella of instance-based approximation with no training phase, and it is suitable for GPU-based parallelisation. A Python GPU-friendly package LipFit which implements the methods discussed is discussed.
tldr: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated method for Lipschitz-continuous scattered data interpolation with monotonicity constraints.
motivation: To provide a fast, parallelizable interpolation method that preserves monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity for large datasets.
method: The method constructs tight upper and lower approximations using local Lipschitz constants and implements them on GPU via Python package LipFit.
result: The approach yields optimal Lipschitz-continuous approximations without discontinuities, suitable for GPU parallelization.
conclusion: LipFit offers an efficient tool for scattered data fitting with monotonicity constraints, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Minimax Private Estimation Of Smooth Optimal-Transport Maps
authors: Cl\'ement Lalanne, David Rodr\'iguez-V\'itores, Franck Iutzeler, Jean-Michel Loubes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of estimating smooth optimal transport (OT) maps between two probability distributions under differential privacy (DP) constraints. Leveraging wavelet-based density estimators and recent stability bounds for smooth OT maps, we propose differentially private estimators that apply to both central and local DP models. Our main estimator achieves near-minimax optimal rates in dimension [MATH], and we complement it with a quantile-based estimator that attains minimax optimal rates in dimension [MATH] under central DP. We further establish matching minimax lower bounds, confirming the near-optimality of our approach. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes the first differentially private procedure for OT map estimation with minimax optimality guarantees.
tldr: This paper develops differentially private estimators for smooth optimal transport maps, achieving near-minimax optimal rates.
motivation: To address privacy concerns in estimating optimal transport maps, which are widely used in data science, by providing the first differentially private procedure with minimax optimality guarantees.
method: The authors use wavelet-based density estimators and stability bounds for smooth OT maps to construct private estimators for both central and local differential privacy models, and derive matching minimax lower bounds.
result: The proposed estimators achieve near-minimax optimal rates in dimension d, with a quantile-based variant attaining minimax optimal rates in dimension 1 under central DP.
conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for private OT map estimation, with implications for privacy-preserving data analysis, though it is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: The No-Core Principle For Stationary Actions And Ends Of Stationary Random Subgroups
authors: Nadav Kalma Yair Hartman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a No-Core Principle for stationary actions of countable groups. Namely, if a Borel set intersects almost every orbit in finitely many points and has positive measure, then it is supported, modulo null sets, on the finite-orbit part of the action. This extends to stationary actions a basic regularity phenomenon known for measure-preserving actions. We apply this principle to the geometry of Stationary Random Subgroups. For a finitely generated group, we prove that the Schreier graph of a stationary random subgroup has almost surely 0,1,2, or infinitely many ends. Finally, we contrast this probabilistic regularity with the topological notion of Boomerang subgroups: for every [MATH], including [MATH], we construct a Boomerang subgroup of [MATH] whose Schreier graph has exactly [MATH] ends.
tldr: The paper proves a No-Core Principle for stationary actions of countable groups and applies it to classify the number of ends of Schreier graphs of stationary random subgroups.
motivation: To extend regularity properties known for measure-preserving actions to stationary actions, and to understand the geometric structure of stationary random subgroups.
method: The authors use ergodic theory and group theory to prove the No-Core Principle, then apply it to analyze the ends of Schreier graphs of stationary random subgroups.
result: The No-Core Principle holds for stationary actions, and the Schreier graph of a stationary random subgroup almost surely has 0, 1, 2, or infinitely many ends. Additionally, they construct Boomerang subgroups with any prescribed number of ends.
conclusion: The work establishes a fundamental regularity for stationary actions and reveals a sharp contrast between probabilistic and topological behavior of subgroups.

title: Near-Optimal Decentralized Stochastic Convex Optimization Over Networks
authors: Nitai Kluger, Amit Attia, Tomer Koren
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study decentralized stochastic smooth convex optimization, where [MATH] workers minimize an average objective using local stochastic gradients and neighbor-only communication over a fixed gossip network. A central question in this setting is to determine the largest number of workers that can be used under a total budget of [MATH] gradient samples while still preserving the centralized [MATH] statistical rate. We introduce an accelerated decentralized method that preserves this rate for up to [MATH] workers, where [MATH] is the spectral gap of the gossip network, improving the best prior maximal scaling of [MATH]. The method is based on a one-step-delayed stochastic acceleration scheme that enables workers to interleave minibatching with accelerated gossip while controlling residual disagreement, and its guarantee depends only logarithmically on the optimum-local heterogeneity. We also establish a matching lower bound for linear-span decentralized first-order methods, showing that the method is optimal up to logarithmic factors.
tldr: This paper studies decentralized stochastic convex optimization over networks, achieving near-optimal scaling with the number of workers.
motivation: To determine the maximum number of workers that can be used in decentralized optimization while preserving the centralized statistical rate.
method: An accelerated decentralized method based on one-step-delayed stochastic acceleration, interleaving minibatching with accelerated gossip.
result: The method preserves the centralized rate for up to O(1/√γ) workers, where γ is the spectral gap, improving over the previous best O(1/γ). A matching lower bound is also established.
conclusion: The method is optimal up to logarithmic factors for linear-span decentralized first-order methods, with implications for large-scale distributed optimization.

title: Dynamic Fdd For Spectrum Sharing In Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Sourav Mukherjee, Bho Matthiesen, Armin Dekorsy, Petar Popovski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Future 6G networks are envisioned to integrate low Earth orbit satellite mega-constellations to enable seamless global connectivity, particularly in underserved and remote areas. However, the deployment of dense mega-constellations introduces interference among satellites operating over shared frequency bands. This represents a rather new setup for studying spectrum sharing, which exacerbates the limited flexibility of conventional FDD systems based on fixed bands for downlink and uplink transmissions. We address this spectrum-sharing problem and propose dynamic re-assignment of FDD bands for improved interference management in dense deployments, as well as evaluate the performance gain of this approach. To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem that incorporates dynamic band assignment, user scheduling, and power allocation in both directions. This non-convex mixed integer problem is solved using a combination of equivalence transforms, alternating optimization, and state-of-the-art industrial-grade mixed integer solvers. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed approach of dynamic FDD band assignment significantly enhances system performance over conventional FDD, achieving up to 30\% improvement in throughput in dense deployments.
tldr: This paper proposes dynamic FDD band assignment for spectrum sharing in non-terrestrial networks to improve throughput in dense satellite deployments.
motivation: Dense LEO satellite constellations cause interference over shared frequency bands, and conventional fixed FDD lacks flexibility to manage this interference effectively.
method: A joint optimization problem combining dynamic band assignment, user scheduling, and power allocation is formulated as a non-convex mixed integer problem, solved via equivalence transforms, alternating optimization, and mixed integer solvers.
result: Dynamic FDD band assignment achieves up to 30% throughput improvement over conventional FDD in dense deployments.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates significant performance gains, suggesting potential for future 6G non-terrestrial networks, though practical implementation challenges remain.

title: An Algebraic Multiscale Preconditioner For Large Sparse Spd Matrices
authors: Yingjie Zhou, Shubin Fu, Eric Tsz Shun Chung
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a two-grid algebraic multiscale preconditioner for large sparse symmetric positive definite systems arising from elliptic problems with highly heterogeneous coefficients. The coarse space is constructed directly from the system matrix by graph partitioning and local generalized eigenvalue solvers, yielding basis functions that capture the low-energy modes responsible for slow convergence. The method requires no geometric information, making it suitable for unstructured and matrix-only settings, and its construction is naturally parallelizable. Numerical results for heterogeneous Darcy flow problems show robustness with respect to coefficient contrast and problem size, better performance than standard algebraic multigrid on challenging large-scale cases, and good parallel scalability.
tldr: This paper presents a two-grid algebraic multiscale preconditioner for large sparse SPD matrices arising from elliptic problems with heterogeneous coefficients, using graph partitioning and local eigenvalue solvers.
motivation: To develop a robust and parallelizable preconditioner for large-scale elliptic problems with high coefficient contrast, without requiring geometric information.
method: Constructs coarse space basis functions via graph partitioning and local generalized eigenvalue problems to capture low-energy modes, forming a two-grid algebraic multiscale preconditioner.
result: Numerical results on heterogeneous Darcy flow show robustness to coefficient contrast and problem size, outperforming standard algebraic multigrid on challenging cases, with good parallel scalability.
conclusion: The method is effective for unstructured and matrix-only settings, with potential for further extension to more complex problems.

title: A Decoupled Energy-stable Mixed Finite Element Method For Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: Yanmei Peng, Ying Yang, Yi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel linearized mixed finite element method for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes (PNPNS) system. Specifically, the method combines a staggered time discretization that eliminates the need for expensive nonlinear solvers by carefully treating nonlinear terms in a time-staggered manner, with a mimetic spatial discretization that preserves the exact structure of the discrete de Rham complex. Both semi-discrete scheme and its fully discrete counterpart are developed, which preserve key physical properties, including conservation of the total mass and energy stability. Under appropriate assumptions on the initial data, a rigorous theoretical analysis is carried out for the fully discrete scheme. Numerical experiments using mimetic spectral elements are presented to demonstrate the properties and to verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed decoupled approach.
tldr: This paper develops a decoupled, energy-stable mixed finite element method for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes system, focusing on numerical analysis and simulation of electrokinetic flows.
motivation: To efficiently solve the coupled PNPNS system while preserving physical properties like mass conservation and energy stability, avoiding expensive nonlinear solvers.
method: A linearized mixed finite element method with staggered time discretization and mimetic spatial discretization that preserves the discrete de Rham complex.
result: The proposed schemes conserve total mass and maintain energy stability; numerical experiments with mimetic spectral elements verify accuracy and effectiveness.
conclusion: The method provides a robust numerical framework for PNPNS systems, with potential applications in electrokinetics and microfluidics.

title: Convergence Of Parallel Overlapping Domain Decomposition Methods With Impedance Boundary Conditions For Time-harmonic Maxwell Equations In Heterogeneous Media
authors: Luyu Cen, Shihua Gong, Euan A. Spence, Yue Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper analyzes the convergence of parallel overlapping domain-decomposition methods with impedance boundary conditions for the time-harmonic Maxwell equations in heterogeneous media. We prove that the parallel iterative method is well-posed in an appropriate function space, and characterize the error propagation operator through impedance-to-impedance maps that describe interactions between neighboring subdomains. For strip domain decompositions, we derive explicit convergence estimates in terms of the norms of the impedance-to-impedance maps. At the discrete level, we develop the finite-element counterpart of these results based on N\'{e}d\'{e}lec-element discretisations. Under the assumption that the discrete impedance-to-impedance maps approximate their continuous counterparts as the mesh is refined, we show that the discrete method inherits the convergence behavior of the continuous method. We illustrate this theory with numerical experiments for strip domain decompositions, and also present numerical experiments for checkerboard domain decompositions that go beyond our theory.
tldr: This paper analyzes convergence of domain decomposition methods for Maxwell equations in heterogeneous media, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To develop rigorous convergence theory for parallel overlapping domain decomposition methods with impedance boundary conditions for time-harmonic Maxwell equations.
method: The authors prove well-posedness of the parallel iterative method, characterize error propagation via impedance-to-impedance maps, derive explicit convergence estimates for strip decompositions, and develop finite-element discretization using Nédélec elements.
result: Explicit convergence estimates are obtained for strip domain decompositions, and numerical experiments confirm the theory for strip and checkerboard decompositions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for domain decomposition methods in heterogeneous media, with potential extensions to more complex geometries.

title: Dual Lyapunov-based Synchronization Control Of R\"ossler System
authors: Alk{\i}m G\"ok\c{c}en, Sava\c{s} \c{s}ahin, Mahmut Kudeyt, Swapnil Tripathi, \"ozkan Karabacak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for the synchronization problem of nonlinear dynamical systems, integrating dual Lyapunov stability analysis with polynomial optimization. A comprehensive review of the relevant scientific literature on synchronization methods is conducted, with a particular focus on classical Lyapunov-based methods for chaotic systems. In this study, the R\"ossler system is synchronized by employing dual Lyapunov-based closed-loop synchronization method. This method uses semidefinite programming and sum-of-squares polynomials to compute a nonlinear state feedback function which synchronize a chaotic system to a selected reference model. It is aimed that chaotic behavior is destroyed and, instead, a limit cycle becomes attracting. Simulation works are performed for randomly selected 100 different initial conditions to show that synchronization process is successfully performed. Furthermore, bifurcation diagrams and phase portraits are evaluated to analyze the system dynamics. The paper discusses results and how new constraints should be employed and adapted to more complex systems.
tldr: This paper uses dual Lyapunov-based synchronization control to synchronize the Rössler system, employing semidefinite programming and sum-of-squares polynomials.
motivation: To develop a novel synchronization method for nonlinear dynamical systems, specifically chaotic systems, by integrating dual Lyapunov stability analysis with polynomial optimization.
method: The method uses dual Lyapunov-based closed-loop synchronization with semidefinite programming and sum-of-squares polynomials to compute a nonlinear state feedback function that synchronizes the chaotic Rössler system to a reference model.
result: Simulations with 100 random initial conditions show successful synchronization, destroying chaotic behavior and attracting a limit cycle; bifurcation diagrams and phase portraits are analyzed.
conclusion: The approach is effective for the Rössler system and can be adapted to more complex systems with new constraints.

title: Learning Control-Affine Reduced-Order Models Via Autoencoders
authors: Martin M\"onnigmann Ali Mjalled
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present in this paper a framework for the identification of control-affine reduced-order models (ROMs). The proposed method utilizes autoencoders (AEs) to transform the high-dimensional states, and potentially the high-dimensional inputs, into reduced latent ones suitable for control-affine state-space dynamics. This is achieved by simultaneous training of the AE and the state-space model. In addition, we extend the discrete ROM formulation to a sequence-based model, which processes state and input histories to improve prediction accuracy while preserving the control-affine structure. We motivate our framework by applying feedback linearization to the derived models, and we present guidelines for its efficient use. The proposed framework is assessed on two numerical examples and its performance is compared to a baseline model, where the AE identifies a latent space with linear state-space dynamics. The assessment involves evaluating the prediction accuracy of the ROM on test data and its effectiveness in controlling the system to a desired state or trajectory.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for learning control-affine reduced-order models using autoencoders, focusing on nonlinear system identification and control.
motivation: To develop a method for identifying reduced-order models that preserve control-affine structure, enabling efficient control of high-dimensional systems.
method: Autoencoders are used to map high-dimensional states and inputs to a latent space, where a control-affine state-space model is learned simultaneously. A sequence-based extension processes state and input histories.
result: The proposed framework outperforms a baseline linear latent-space model in prediction accuracy and control effectiveness on two numerical examples.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to obtain control-affine ROMs suitable for feedback linearization, with potential for broader application in nonlinear control.

title: Adaptive Sequential Change Detection Using Mixtures Of Predictive Distributions
authors: Topi Halme, H. Vincent Poor, Visa Koivunen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the problem of detecting a change in the distribution of a sequence of independent observations when the post-change distribution is unknown. We propose a novel change detection algorithm, termed Predictive-Mixture CuSum (PM-CuSum), which combines predictive distributions constructed from sliding windows of different lengths within a CuSum recursion. The predictive distributions are aggregated using adaptive weights based on their recent predictive performance. We show that PM-CuSum achieves first-order asymptotic optimality under mild conditions, and that its asymptotic delay bound has a smaller remainder order than what is achieved by any fixed (even oracle) window. Numerical simulations demonstrate that PM-CuSum performs well compared to existing methods. Moreover, it is demonstrated that forming likelihood ratios using full predictive distributions can substantially improve performance compared to plug-in likelihoods.
tldr: This paper proposes a change detection algorithm (PM-CuSum) for detecting distribution changes in independent observations when the post-change distribution is unknown, using adaptive mixtures of predictive distributions.
motivation: To address the problem of detecting changes in distribution when the post-change distribution is unknown, which is common in many applications.
method: The PM-CuSum algorithm combines predictive distributions from sliding windows of different lengths within a CuSum recursion, with adaptive weights based on recent predictive performance.
result: PM-CuSum achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and has a smaller asymptotic delay bound remainder than any fixed window method; numerical simulations show good performance.
conclusion: The method improves change detection performance, especially when using full predictive distributions instead of plug-in likelihoods, with potential applications in sequential analysis.

title: Bregman Divergences And Error Control Via Convex Duality
authors: P. A. Gazca-Orozco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convex duality relations are a useful tool for deriving error estimates for challenging nonlinear and non-smooth variational problems. Applied at the continuous level they can deliver nonlinear analogues of the Prager-Synge a posteriori error identity, while at the discrete level they allow the derivation of minimal regularity a priori estimates. By leveraging elementary properties of Bregman divergences, we obtain three results on the error control via convex duality for a general class of problems: first, we prove a local efficiency bound for the duality gap error estimator, secondly, we derive a guaranteed a posteriori bound for non-conforming fields, and finally, we prove a minimal-regularity quasioptimal estimate for a Crouzeix-Raviart discretisation of the [MATH]-Laplace problem.
tldr: This paper uses convex duality and Bregman divergences to derive error estimates for nonlinear variational problems, with applications to the p-Laplace problem.
motivation: To develop error control techniques for challenging nonlinear and non-smooth variational problems where standard methods fail.
method: Leverages elementary properties of Bregman divergences and convex duality relations to derive a posteriori and a priori error estimates.
result: Proves a local efficiency bound for the duality gap error estimator, a guaranteed a posteriori bound for non-conforming fields, and a minimal-regularity quasioptimal estimate for a Crouzeix-Raviart discretisation of the p-Laplace problem.
conclusion: The results provide robust error control for a general class of problems, with potential extensions to other nonlinear PDEs.

title: Bayesian Membership Privacy For Graph Neural Networks
authors: Megha Khosla Sinan Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m
