By studying the structure of these algebras, we find all factorizable solutions. Finally, we study the structure of \(A\)-generalized Hessian pre-Lie algebras. In particular, we obtain a structural description via central and double extensions and classify low-dimensional non-trivial \(A\)-generalized Hessian pre-Lie algebras.
tldr: This paper introduces A-generalized Hessian pre-Lie algebras and A-generalized Yang-Baxter equations, studying their symmetric and factorizable solutions.
motivation: The research was motivated by the problem of constructing pre-Lie algebra structures on the dual space of a pre-Lie algebra.
method: The authors define A-generalized Yang-Baxter equations and study their solutions through A-generalized Hessian pre-Lie algebras, classifying solutions into symmetric and factorizable types, and establishing correspondences with generalized quadratic Rota-Baxter pre-Lie algebras.
result: Key findings include a one-to-one correspondence between factorizable solutions and generalized quadratic Rota-Baxter pre-Lie algebras of nonzero weight, and a structural description of A-generalized Hessian pre-Lie algebras via central and double extensions, with classification of low-dimensional nontrivial examples.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding pre-Lie algebra structures and their duals, with potential applications in algebra and mathematical physics, though no direct connections to the user's research interests are evident.

title: Reduced Order Modeling For Spatio-temporal Pattern Approximation In Diffusive Lotka-Volterra Equations
authors: Murat Uzunca B\"ulent Karas\"ozen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an efficient reduced order modeling (ROM) framework for simulating spatio-temporal pattern formation in three-species diffusive Lotka-Volterra systems. To alleviate the high computational cost associated with long-time simulations of the high-dimensional full order model (FOM), we apply proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to project the solution onto a low-dimensional subspace. Further efficiency is achieved through tensorial POD (TPOD), which preserves the quadratic nonlinear structure and enables offline-online decomposition. Numerical experiments demonstrate that both POD and TPOD accurately replicate the key features of spatial segregation patterns while substantially reducing computation time, whereas the TPOD is faster. Additionally, we demonstrate accurate long-time pattern prediction using limited training data.
tldr: This paper applies reduced order modeling (POD/TPOD) to simulate pattern formation in diffusive Lotka-Volterra equations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To reduce computational cost of long-time simulations of high-dimensional diffusive Lotka-Volterra systems.
method: Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and tensorial POD (TPOD) are used to project the full order model onto a low-dimensional subspace, preserving quadratic nonlinearity.
result: Both POD and TPOD accurately replicate spatial segregation patterns while significantly reducing computation time, with TPOD being faster.
conclusion: The ROM framework enables efficient long-time pattern prediction with limited training data, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: On The First Caustic Of Elliptical Billiards
authors: Aleksandra Uskova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A point source of light is placed inside a billiard with a smooth, convex, closed boundary. For any integer [MATH], the [MATH]-th caustic by reflection, denoted by [MATH], is the envelope of light rays that have undergone [MATH] reflections in such a billiard after emanating from the source. It has been conjectured by Gil Bor and Serge Tabachnikov that for an elliptical billiard, [MATH] has exactly four ordinary cusps; this problem is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement, which concerns the number of cusps in the conjugate locus of a point on an ellipsoid. Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, and Serge Tabachnikov have proven that [MATH] has at least four ordinary cusps. In this paper, we present a proof that [MATH] has exactly four ordinary cusps, using billiards in complex spaces.
tldr: This paper proves that the first caustic by reflection in an elliptical billiard has exactly four ordinary cusps, resolving a conjecture related to Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement.
motivation: To prove a conjecture about the number of cusps in the first caustic of an elliptical billiard, which is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement.
method: The proof uses billiards in complex spaces to analyze the envelope of light rays after one reflection.
result: The first caustic by reflection in an elliptical billiard has exactly four ordinary cusps.
conclusion: The result confirms the conjecture and provides a complete solution to this geometric problem, with potential implications for billiard dynamics and optics.

title: An Efficient Solver For The Richards Equation For Variably Saturated Flows In Porous Media
authors: Qi Wang Xuelong Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a nonlinear multigrid solver for the Richards equation in variably saturated porous media with strongly nonlinear hydraulic conductivity and water-retention relationships. The governing equation is discretized using a second-order conservative finite-difference scheme in space and an implicit backward differentiation formula in time. The core component of the solver is a nonlinear Gauss--Seidel (NGS) smoother based on a triangular splitting of the diffusion operator combined with diagonal stabilization. This construction yields a sequence of locally decoupled scalar nonlinear problems that can be solved efficiently and robustly using only a few Newton iterations. Under suitable monotonicity assumptions, we establish the convergence of the NGS iteration in the [MATH] norm and derive explicit conditions on the stabilization parameters. Numerical experiments for benchmark infiltration, drainage, and root-uptake problems demonstrate that the proposed NGS-based multigrid framework is both computationally efficient and robust.
tldr: This paper presents a nonlinear multigrid solver for the Richards equation in variably saturated porous media, focusing on computational efficiency and robustness.
motivation: To efficiently solve the strongly nonlinear Richards equation for variably saturated flows in porous media, which is important in hydrology and geoscience.
method: A nonlinear multigrid solver with a nonlinear Gauss-Seidel smoother based on triangular splitting and diagonal stabilization, discretized with second-order finite differences and implicit time stepping.
result: The solver converges under monotonicity assumptions and demonstrates computational efficiency and robustness on benchmark infiltration, drainage, and root-uptake problems.
conclusion: The proposed solver is efficient and robust for strongly nonlinear problems, with potential for further application in porous media flow simulations.

title: Decoupled Iterative Schemes For Solving Stationary Mhd Problems
authors: Driss Yakoubi Aziz Takhirov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a novel iterative approach for solving the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics problem. The main idea is to split the velocity-momentum and magnetic induction equations with respect to the diffusive terms. As a result, we get a smaller system that is iteration-level-dependent, along with two Stokes systems that need to be assembled only once. We also extended the scheme to the Els{\"a}sser variables reformulation of the equations. For both schemes, we established boundedness and convergence. Several numerical experiments are presented to show the effectiveness of the schemes.
tldr: This paper develops iterative numerical schemes for solving stationary magnetohydrodynamics problems, focusing on decoupling velocity and magnetic field equations.
motivation: To improve computational efficiency and convergence of numerical methods for incompressible MHD problems.
method: Splits the velocity-momentum and magnetic induction equations with respect to diffusive terms, leading to smaller iteration-dependent systems and two Stokes systems assembled once.
result: Established boundedness and convergence of the schemes; numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed decoupled iterative schemes offer a computationally efficient approach for stationary MHD problems, with potential extensions to Elsässer variables.

title: Rigidity Phenomena For Time Changes Of Products Of Anosov Flows
authors: Miri Son Amadeus Maldonado
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our main results establish two rigidity phenomena in the class of time changes of a fixed product of Anosov flows. Our first result shows that two time changes having the same stabilizers for all periodic orbits are conjugate up to automorphism. The second rigidity result proves that if the stabilizers of periodic orbits can be simultaneously diagonalized, then the time change is conjugate to a product of flows up to automorphism. We allow our time changes to be H\"older continuous, which by structural stability implies that our results hold for [MATH] perturbations of products of Anosov flows. We apply our main results to [MATH] time changes of products of Anosov flows on [MATH]-dimensional manifolds. For such actions, we show that being totally Anosov, being conjugate to a product of flows and having the kernels of Lyapunov functionals not depend on the periodic orbits are all equivalent properties. We also build counterexamples to the Katok-Spatzier conjecture as time changes of products of any transitive Anosov flows, extending a result of Vinhage beyond the continuously accessible case.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity phenomena for time changes of products of Anosov flows, a topic in dynamical systems, with no connection to quantum information or condensed matter physics.
motivation: To establish rigidity results for time changes of Anosov flows and to build counterexamples to the Katok-Spatzier conjecture.
method: The authors use dynamical systems theory, including analysis of stabilizers of periodic orbits and Lyapunov functionals, and apply structural stability to extend results to Hölder continuous perturbations.
result: Two rigidity results: (1) time changes with same stabilizers for all periodic orbits are conjugate up to automorphism; (2) if stabilizers can be simultaneously diagonalized, the time change is conjugate to a product of flows. Also, counterexamples to the Katok-Spatzier conjecture are constructed.
conclusion: The results contribute to the classification of time changes of Anosov flows and have implications for the Katok-Spatzier conjecture, but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Penalized Order Selection For Arfima Models
authors: Chunhao Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study order selection for a finite-order stationary ARFIMA process by minimizing a nested folded-concave penalization of the integrated Toeplitz profile Whittle criterion. The AR and MA orders are encoded through suffix groups, so that exact recovery of the zero tails is equivalent to exact recovery of the orders. The analysis is carried out on a weighted sieve neighborhood whose geometric weights keep growing-lag perturbations from pushing AR or MA roots toward the unit circle. Under finite true orders, coprime root-separated short-memory polynomials, an interior stationary memory parameter, growing sieve orders, suitable tuning, and independent sub-Gaussian innovations, we prove existence of an oracle local minimizer, rather than global optimality of the nonconvex criterion. This local minimizer selects the true AR and MA orders with probability tending to one, sets all inactive coefficients exactly to zero, and achieves the active-coordinate rate \( \Op(L_n n^{-1/2}) \), where the stochastic scale \(L_n\) is governed by the local mismatch \(\Delta\). The proof combines weighted root-separation, matched finite-section Toeplitz control, finite-section trace-bias control, a sub-Gaussian quadratic-form argument for the stationary observed vector, and a local domination step for folded-concave penalties.
tldr: This paper proposes a penalized order selection method for ARFIMA time series models, which is unrelated to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.
motivation: To improve order selection for ARFIMA models in time series analysis.
method: Minimization of a nested folded-concave penalized integrated Toeplitz profile Whittle criterion with weighted sieve neighborhoods.
result: Proves existence of an oracle local minimizer that selects true orders with probability tending to one and achieves active-coordinate rate.
conclusion: Provides theoretical guarantees for order selection in ARFIMA models, but no direct implications for the user's research interests.

title: Intermingled Basins: Kan's Example On The Riemann Sphere
authors: Abbas Fakhari, Ale Jan Homburg, Sebastian van Strien
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kan's discovery of dynamical systems with two attractors whose basins of attraction both have full support, featured specific examples of skew product systems of interval diffeomorphisms forced by expanding circle maps. The interval diffeomorphisms are polynomial maps and can hence be considered on the Riemann sphere. We consider the resulting skew product systems of holomorphic maps on the Riemann sphere forced by expanding circle maps, and establish the existence of three attractors whose basins of attraction all have full support and are thus intermingled.
tldr: This paper studies intermingled basins of attraction in skew product systems of holomorphic maps on the Riemann sphere, extending Kan's example.
motivation: To understand dynamical systems with multiple attractors whose basins are topologically large (full support) and intermingled, a phenomenon first discovered by Kan for interval maps.
method: The authors construct skew product systems of holomorphic maps on the Riemann sphere forced by expanding circle maps, and analyze the basins of attraction.
result: They establish the existence of three attractors whose basins of attraction all have full support and are intermingled.
conclusion: This work extends Kan's example to a holomorphic setting on the Riemann sphere, contributing to the theory of intermingled basins and complex dynamics.

title: Arbitrary High Order Shaped Stencils For Time Domain Finite Difference Schemes In Seismic Wave Propagation
authors: Felipe A. G. Silva Pedro S. Peixto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite Difference Schemes are widely used in the approximation of different hyperbolic (wave-like) differential equations, and are particularly important for seismic wave modelling and its applications. Classical methods based on Taylor Series are dominant in the literature; however, it is known that these methods can suffer from excessive numerical dispersion. In this paper, we review and extend existing high-order in space finite difference schemes for acoustic wave propagation, featuring different stencil geometries ranging from classical cross stencils to stencils with rhombus or square-like shapes, and propose a general mathematical framework for their derivation. The numerical implementation is performed in a symbolic, high-level framework (Devito), which compiles and runs highly optimized, stencil-based computations, allowing for a low-level interpretation of the methods efficiency. We demonstrate that non-cross stencil shapes, such as rhombus and square-based stencils, do not necessarily provide added accuracy or dispersion reduction in general, despite their increased computational cost. However, results on both idealized and realistic velocity models confirm the benefits of using dispersion-optimized cross-stencils, indicating adequate accuracy with reduced computational cost on more compact stencils compared to classic approaches. Finally, our implementation of the methods provides ease of use for full-scale acoustic seismic inversion problems using Devito.
tldr: This paper presents high-order finite difference schemes for seismic wave propagation, focusing on stencil shapes and dispersion optimization.
motivation: To improve accuracy and reduce numerical dispersion in seismic wave modeling, which is critical for geophysical applications.
method: The authors review and extend high-order finite difference schemes with various stencil geometries (cross, rhombus, square) and implement them using the Devito symbolic framework.
result: Non-cross stencils do not provide added accuracy despite higher cost; dispersion-optimized cross-stencils offer better accuracy with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed cross-stencil methods are efficient for full-scale acoustic seismic inversion, with implementation ease in Devito.

title: Witness-split + Window-cardinality Refinement For $r_3(N)$: Architecture, Empirical Results, And A Structural Hard Pocket
authors: Mehmet Ergezer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a reproducible computational framework for upper-bound searches on r_3(N), the maximum size of a 3-term-arithmetic-progression-free subset of [1,N]. The framework combines a verified lower-bound witness, endpoint forcing, depth-d witness-variable splitting, OEIS A003002 window-cardinality pruning, and recursive refinement of timed-out subproblems. Applied to the frontier case N = 212, K = 44, it found no feasible 44-set across millions of CP-SAT subproblems, supporting but not proving the conjectural value r_3(212) = 43. A 300-second recap leaves 45 resistant chunks; one-hour HiGHS MIP closes none of them; the full eight-hour HiGHS audit closes 25/45 and leaves 20/45 with dual bounds still pinned at 0.0. A CDCL/SAT re-attack on those LP-paradigm-resistant chunks closes 18 via conflict-driven clause learning; all eighteen carry independently verified DRAT proofs. The remaining two chunks (T1c) resist every tested paradigm under generous wall caps. We release the witness, solver scripts, result logs, tiered benchmark instances, verified DRAT/LRAT proofs, and a Lean formal-proof-search encoding of T1c, and frame the unit-gap problem r_3(212) in {43,44} as a target for stronger additive-combinatorial bounds, custom branch-and-bound, or formal proof-search systems.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework for upper-bound searches on r_3(N), the maximum size of a 3-term-arithmetic-progression-free subset, with empirical results for N=212.
motivation: To determine the exact value of r_3(212), which is conjectured to be 43, by combining multiple computational techniques.
method: Combines witness-variable splitting, window-cardinality pruning, CP-SAT, MIP, and CDCL/SAT solvers with DRAT proofs to search for feasible 44-sets.
result: No feasible 44-set found across millions of subproblems; 18 of 45 resistant chunks solved via CDCL, leaving 2 unsolved chunks (T1c).
conclusion: The results support but do not prove r_3(212)=43; the remaining unsolved chunks are targets for stronger methods.

title: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks For Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models
authors: Yingzi Ma, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Minhui Xue, Yue Zhao, Chaowei Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising partially masked sequences under bidirectional context, exposing a safety surface distinct from autoregressive LLMs. Because mask tokens are native inputs and tokens are committed by confidence rather than position, harmful content can be induced through infilling and outside the monitored prefix. Existing jailbreaks either miss this native infill capability or rely on low-diversity mask-bearing templates applied uniformly across goals, with little structural adaptation or accumulated attack experience. We propose MaskForge, a fully black-box adaptive attack that casts dLLM red-teaming as optimized search over a growing library of structural patterns. MaskForge abstracts successful attempts into reusable schemas, selects goal-compatible patterns with a UCB bandit, and invokes a scorer-guided fallback when the current library fails. Successful attempts are distilled back into the pattern library, enabling experience to accumulate across goals. Across five public dLLMs and three benchmarks, MaskForge achieves an average attack success rate of 79.3%, a 17.6% relative improvement over the strongest competing dLLM baseline. The matured pattern library further transfers to AdvBench without any updates, achieving a 88.2% attack success rate and a 67% relative improvement over the strongest competing baseline.
tldr: MaskForge is a black-box adaptive attack method for jailbreaking diffusion large language models, achieving high attack success rates through structural pattern search and experience accumulation.
motivation: Existing jailbreaks for diffusion LLMs either ignore native infill capabilities or use low-diversity templates without structural adaptation, limiting effectiveness.
method: MaskForge uses a UCB bandit to select goal-compatible structural patterns from a growing library, with a scorer-guided fallback when patterns fail, and distills successful attempts back into the library.
result: Achieves 79.3% average attack success rate on five dLLMs, 17.6% relative improvement over baselines, and transfers to AdvBench with 88.2% ASR and 67% relative improvement.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates that adaptive structural attacks can effectively exploit dLLM vulnerabilities, and the pattern library enables transferable attacks.

title: MimeLens: Position-Agnostic Content-Type Detection For Binary Fragments
authors: Michael J. Bommarito II
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: File-type classification underlies many workflows like malware triage, forensic carving, packet inspection, and storage indexing. Learned systems such as Google's Magika assume whole-file access at a known offset, so they break on the inputs many of these tasks actually produce, like a single packet payload, a header-less carved fragment, a random disk block, or a chunked upload. We introduce MimeLens, a family of small BERT-style encoders pretrained on binary content from windows sampled at a uniformly random offset within each file, with no privileged head-of-file position, in standard- and short-context variants. A byte chunk goes in from anywhere in a file, no header needed and no fixed size; out comes one of libmagic's 125 MIME labels. On the clean head of complete files, MimeLens beats Magika v1.1 by +10.7 pp top-1 on libmagic-labeled data, and it keeps classifying where Magika cannot: from a single mid-stream UDP packet, and more than twice as accurately as libmagic and Magika on random mid-file disk blocks. The cost is latency: MimeLens runs roughly one to two orders of magnitude slower per sample on CPU than Magika, though it matches on consumer GPUs or in batch. All trained checkpoints are released on Hugging Face (mjbommar/mimelens-001-*).
tldr: MimeLens is a BERT-style model for content-type detection of binary fragments without requiring file headers or fixed offsets.
motivation: Existing file-type classifiers assume whole-file access at known offsets, failing on fragmented inputs like packet payloads or disk blocks.
method: Pretrained small BERT-style encoders on binary content from random offsets within files, then fine-tuned for 125 MIME label classification.
result: Outperforms Magika on clean file heads and classifies mid-stream fragments where Magika fails, but is slower on CPU.
conclusion: MimeLens enables robust file-type classification for fragmented data, with trade-offs in latency; useful for malware triage and forensic carving.

title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts For Ai Agent Actions
authors: Juan Figuera
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current AI agent observability is structurally compromised: the entity producing the activity log is the same entity whose activity is being logged. A compromised or buggy agent can omit, alter, or fabricate its own traces, and the operator running the agent has no independent way to detect tampering. We propose a class of protocols that resolves this by inverting the trust boundary: the service that receives an agent's call signs a receipt of what it observed using its own key, encrypts the receipt to the agent's owner, and publishes it to a public transparency log. The owner reconstructs a tamper-evident trail without trusting the agent or its operator. We instantiate the class as Sello, a protocol combining four properties absent in any current system: (P1) receiver-side signing, (P2) HPKE encryption to an owner public key bound to the authorization token via JWS, (P3) publication to a witness-cosigned Merkle log, and (P4) owner-side discovery by token reference. We describe the protocol, analyze its security under an adversary that controls the agent and its operator, present microbenchmarks of the cryptographic operations, and situate Sello among adjacent receipt-protocol work (Signet, AgentROA, Agent Passport System, draft-farley-acta, SCITT). We discuss known limitations including the suppression attack, service collusion, and the adoption-incentive problem.
tldr: This paper proposes a protocol for tamper-evident logging of AI agent actions using receiver-signed receipts and public transparency logs.
motivation: Current AI agent observability is compromised because the agent itself produces the activity log, allowing tampering. The research aims to provide independent verification of agent actions.
method: The protocol, Sello, combines receiver-side signing, HPKE encryption to an owner public key, publication to a witness-cosigned Merkle log, and owner-side discovery by token reference.
result: The protocol achieves tamper-evident trails without trusting the agent or its operator, with microbenchmarks showing feasible cryptographic overhead.
conclusion: Sello addresses a critical security gap in AI agent observability, though it faces limitations like suppression attacks and service collusion.

title: Formal Verification Of The S-two Air
authors: Jeremy Avigad, Anat Ganor, Lior Goldberg, David Levit, Ohad Nir, Yoav Seginer, Alon Titelman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: StarkWare's S-two prover provides an efficient means for establishing, on blockchain, that a program written in the Cairo virtual machine language runs to completion. The latter claim is encoded by an algebraic intermediate representation (AIR) that captures the semantics of the Cairo language. The AIR asserts the existence of tables of values from a finite field satisfying certain algebraic constraints. A cryptographic interactive proof system, circle STARK, provides an efficiently-checked certificate that the AIR is satisfied. We describe our verification, using the Lean 4 proof assistant, that the AIR encoding is sound, which is to say, the satisfiability of the AIR implies the computational claim.
tldr: This paper presents a formal verification of the soundness of an algebraic intermediate representation (AIR) used in StarkWare's S-two prover for blockchain program execution.
motivation: To ensure the correctness and security of blockchain computations by formally proving that the AIR encoding correctly captures the semantics of the Cairo virtual machine language.
method: The authors used the Lean 4 proof assistant to formally verify that satisfiability of the AIR implies the computational claim about program execution.
result: The verification confirms that the AIR encoding is sound, meaning that if the AIR constraints are satisfied, the original program claim holds.
conclusion: This work enhances trust in blockchain provers and demonstrates the feasibility of formal verification for complex cryptographic protocols.

title: Toward A Generalized Defense Across Sparse, Continuous, And Structured Parameter Attacks
authors: Bin Duan, Zeyu Bai, Guowei Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep neural networks are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous and partially untrusted environments, where models are distributed through cloud storage, CI/CD pipelines, containerized services, and edge execution platforms. This broad deployment landscape exposes model parameters to various integrity risks. Unlike input-space adversarial attacks, parameter attacks directly tamper with the model's internal parameters and persist across all subsequent inferences. Existing defenses either require retraining, incur significant accuracy degradation, or are limited to specific attack classes. However, in real-world deployment scenarios, the forms of parameter attacks are often unpredictable. To address this challenge, we present ParDef, a generalized defense for deep neural networks against diverse types of parameter attacks. ParDef integrates keyed channel reparameterization, which obscures sensitive parameter directions, QC-LDPC quantization, which embeds redundancy and supports error correction, and adaptive robust inference, which stabilizes predictions under uncertainty. Our evaluation on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet using ResNet and VGG models demonstrates that ParDef consistently reduces attack success rates across different parameter attacks while maintaining high model performance and incurring only moderate deployment overhead. These results highlight that ParDef is a practical and generalized defense for DNN deployments.
tldr: ParDef is a generalized defense for deep neural networks against parameter tampering attacks, using keyed channel reparameterization, QC-LDPC quantization, and adaptive robust inference.
motivation: Deep neural networks deployed in heterogeneous environments face integrity risks from parameter attacks, which existing defenses cannot handle comprehensively.
method: ParDef combines keyed channel reparameterization to obscure sensitive parameters, QC-LDPC quantization for error correction, and adaptive robust inference to stabilize predictions.
result: On CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet with ResNet and VGG models, ParDef consistently reduces attack success rates while maintaining high accuracy and moderate overhead.
conclusion: ParDef provides a practical generalized defense for DNNs against diverse parameter attacks, with potential for further optimization and deployment.

title: From Untrusted Input To Trusted Memory: A Systematic Study Of Memory Poisoning Attacks In Llm Agents
authors: Pritam Dash, Tongyu Ge, Aditi Jain, Tanmay Shah, Zhiwei Shang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory is a core component of AI agents, enabling them to accumulate knowledge across interactions and improve performance. However, persistent memory introduces the risk of memory poisoning, where a single adversarial memory write can exert long-term influence over agent behavior. We present a systematic study of memory poisoning in LLM-based agents. We identify four memory write channels and nine structural vulnerabilities in model capabilities, system prompt design, and agent system architecture that make these channels exploitable. Based on these vulnerabilities, we develop a taxonomy of six classes of memory poisoning attacks. Furthermore, we design MPBench -- a benchmark for evaluating memory poisoning attacks, and show that agents designed to write and retrieve memory more aggressively are more exploitable. We also show that existing prompt injection defenses fail to cover memory poisoning attacks. Our findings provide a foundation for understanding and mitigating memory poisoning attacks against AI agents.
tldr: This paper studies memory poisoning attacks in LLM-based agents, focusing on security vulnerabilities rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To systematically understand and categorize memory poisoning attacks in LLM agents, which pose long-term security risks.
method: Identifies memory write channels and structural vulnerabilities, develops a taxonomy of attack classes, and creates a benchmark (MPBench) for evaluation.
result: Agents with aggressive memory write/retrieval are more exploitable; existing prompt injection defenses are insufficient against memory poisoning.
conclusion: The findings provide a foundation for developing defenses against memory poisoning in AI agents.

title: Pepper: High-bandwidth And Scalable Anonymous Broadcast With Cryptographic Privacy
authors: Chenghao Li, Haoyuan Wang, Xianghang Mi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Pepper, a high-bandwidth anonymous broadcast protocol that provides cryptographic sender anonymity against global adversaries. Pepper builds on a two-server DC-net architecture but introduces three key innovations: a self-contained anonymous registration subprotocol using verifiable distributed point functions, support for batch messaging via distributed multi-point functions, and a lightweight access control mechanism based on secret-shared proofs. Unlike prior systems, Pepper eliminates the need for external dialing services and allows each broadcaster to send multiple messages per epoch with a single audit, significantly improving throughput for large data transfers. Our implementation demonstrates that Pepper achieves millisecond-level registration audits, scales efficiently to thousands of channels, and delivers 1.2--20[MATH] higher effective messaging rates than state-of-the-art alternatives. Furthermore, Pepper is designed for practical deployment, with natural compatibility for co-deployment alongside Tor and federated social networks.
tldr: Pepper is a high-bandwidth anonymous broadcast protocol using a two-server DC-net architecture with cryptographic sender anonymity.
motivation: Existing anonymous broadcast systems suffer from low bandwidth, scalability issues, or reliance on external services. Pepper aims to provide high throughput and scalability while maintaining strong anonymity.
method: Pepper introduces a self-contained anonymous registration subprotocol using verifiable distributed point functions, support for batch messaging via distributed multi-point functions, and a lightweight access control mechanism based on secret-shared proofs.
result: Pepper achieves millisecond-level registration audits, scales to thousands of channels, and delivers 1.2–20× higher effective messaging rates than state-of-the-art alternatives.
conclusion: Pepper demonstrates practical deployment potential, with compatibility for co-deployment alongside Tor and federated social networks, offering a scalable solution for anonymous broadcast.

title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark For Ai Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities
authors: Tianneng Shi, Robin Rheem, Dongwei Jiang, Mona Wang, Francisco de la Riega, Zhun Wang, Jingzhi Jiang, Alexander Cheung, Sean Tai, Jonah Cha, Jianhong Tu, Gabriel Han, Chenguang Wang, Jingxuan He, Wenbo Guo, Dawn Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI has the potential to transform cybersecurity by enabling systems that can autonomously detect, analyze, and remediate software vulnerabilities. However, existing cybersecurity evaluations of AI systems are limited in scale or scope, and fail to capture the end-to-end lifecycle of real-world software vulnerability discovery and remediation. To address this gap, we propose CyberGym-E2E, a large-scale and realistic end-to-end cybersecurity benchmark that comprehensively evaluates AI agents' abilities across the full lifecycle of vulnerability discovery, PoC generation, and patch generation. CyberGym-E2E is comprehensive and scalable, as we build an automated, agent-enhanced pipeline for transforming open-source vulnerability data into realistic evaluation environments. Currently, the benchmark consists of 920 real-world vulnerabilities across 139 different open-source projects.
tldr: CyberGym-E2E is a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on end-to-end cybersecurity tasks, unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: Existing cybersecurity evaluations of AI are limited in scale and scope, failing to capture the full vulnerability lifecycle.
method: An automated pipeline transforms open-source vulnerability data into realistic evaluation environments, creating 920 vulnerabilities across 139 projects.
result: The benchmark enables comprehensive assessment of AI agents' abilities in vulnerability discovery, PoC generation, and patch generation.
conclusion: CyberGym-E2E provides a scalable, realistic benchmark for advancing AI in cybersecurity, but is not relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ps-uie: Privilege-Separated Integrity Enforcement For User-Space Executable Objects In Confidential VMs
authors: Xiaolin Chang Jingkai Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs), such as AMD SEV-SNP, enable cloud tenants to run security-sensitive workloads, but tenants can rely on the execution of these workloads only when they can trust the CVM. This trust requires continuous integrity assurance from CVM launch to the current runtime state, including initial trust establishment at launch and subsequent runtime integrity assurance. Existing works help establish launch-time trust and protect parts of runtime integrity, but they do not fully address the integrity of file-backed user-space executable objects, such as main executables, program interpreters, and dynamically loaded shared objects, that may be loaded or mapped dynamically during execution inside CVMs. In this paper, we propose Privilege-Separated User-space Integrity Enforcement (PS-UIE), an approach for enforcing the integrity of user-space executable objects inside AMD SEV-SNP-based CVMs. PS-UIE consists of a privilege-separated architecture and three mechanisms. The architecture separates the authority for integrity measurement and enforcement from the measured targets by placing it in a higher-privileged protected domain. Built on this architecture, PS-UIE provides policy lifecycle management, execution-time integrity enforcement, and evidence export and verification mechanisms. It enables policy-controlled integrity measurement and enforcement for user-space executable objects and generates verifiable runtime evidence. We implement PS-UIE on an AMD SEV-SNP platform. The security analysis and performance evaluation show that PS-UIE enforces the integrity of user-space executable objects on the covered execute-permission grant paths and provides verifiable runtime evidence while incurring acceptable overhead.
tldr: This paper proposes a privilege-separated integrity enforcement mechanism for user-space executables in confidential VMs, focusing on cloud security rather than quantum computing or information thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing integrity assurance methods for confidential VMs do not fully address runtime integrity of dynamically loaded user-space executables, which is critical for trust in cloud environments.
method: The authors design a privilege-separated architecture with three mechanisms: policy lifecycle management, execution-time integrity enforcement, and evidence export/verification, implemented on AMD SEV-SNP.
result: PS-UIE enforces integrity of user-space executable objects on execute-permission grant paths and generates verifiable runtime evidence with acceptable overhead.
conclusion: The approach enhances trust in confidential VMs, but its relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: TIBlender: Early-Warning Threat Intelligence From Cross-Platform Social Media Evidence
authors: Hiroki Nakano, Takashi Koide, Daiki Chiba
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber threat signals are fragmented across multiple social media platforms, yet no existing approach has fully automated their integration into actionable threat intelligence (TI) reports. We present TIBlender, a multi-agent system that monitors four platforms (X, Reddit, Telegram, and Discord) and produces structured TI reports via role-specialized LLM agents. These agents conduct multi-perspective investigations, tracing chains of evidence to uncover related Indicators of Compromise (IoCs) via collaborative, evidence-backed analysis. In a real-world deployment, TIBlender detected emerging threats across all four threat categories ahead of public feeds, including in-the-wild exploitation ahead of public vulnerability registries; the majority of its IoCs were absent from each evaluated feed. Quantitative evaluation confirms that each platform contributes unique threat information unavailable from the others, and that excluding any single platform results in substantial loss of reports in specific threat categories. Under identical single-platform input conditions, TIBlender's IoC extraction meets or exceeds each baseline; the full pipeline surfaces substantially more IoCs, most of which are absent from any single-platform baseline. These results establish cross-platform social media monitoring as an effective and scalable early-warning layer for operational TI pipelines.
tldr: TIBlender is a multi-agent system that integrates threat intelligence from multiple social media platforms using LLM agents.
motivation: Cyber threat signals are scattered across platforms, and no existing method fully automates their integration into actionable reports.
method: The system uses role-specialized LLM agents to monitor X, Reddit, Telegram, and Discord, conducting multi-perspective investigations and evidence-backed analysis.
result: In real-world deployment, TIBlender detected emerging threats ahead of public feeds, and most of its IoCs were absent from existing feeds.
conclusion: Cross-platform social media monitoring is an effective early-warning layer for operational threat intelligence pipelines.

title: TeleHunt: A Framework And Tool For Efficient Cybercriminal Community Discovery On Telegram
authors: Roy Ricaldi, Victor Asanache, Luca Allodi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents TeleHunt, a framework and tool for evaluating the effectiveness of different strategies to discover cybercriminal communities on Telegram. TeleHunt employs a set of reference-driven snowballing strategies, integrating message-level classification, contextual filtering, and market-segment labeling. Using open- and dark-web seeds, we systematically evaluate how seed source, pointer type, and exploration strategy influence discovery outcomes in three dimensions: efficiency, accessibility, and rediscovery. Our work provides (i) a modular cybercrime content discovery pipeline, (ii) the first systematic comparison of Telegram discovery strategies with an empirical characterization of market-segment accessibility, and (iii) a labeled dataset of over 172 million messages from 6,022 Telegram communities.
tldr: TeleHunt is a framework for discovering cybercriminal communities on Telegram using snowballing strategies and message classification.
motivation: To systematically evaluate different strategies for discovering cybercriminal communities on Telegram, addressing the lack of comparative studies in this area.
method: The framework uses reference-driven snowballing with message-level classification, contextual filtering, and market-segment labeling, applied to open- and dark-web seeds.
result: The study provides a modular pipeline, the first systematic comparison of Telegram discovery strategies, and a labeled dataset of over 172 million messages from 6,022 communities.
conclusion: The work offers tools and insights for cybercrime community discovery, with implications for law enforcement and cybersecurity research.

title: Selection-Aware Diagnostics For Chain-of-Thought Answer Hijacking
authors: Jianwei Tai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a controlled numeric proxy for chain-of-thought (CoT) answer hijacking, motivated by attacks in which benign-looking reasoning steers a harmful final answer. CoT wrappers on GSM8K and MATH-500 flip final answers away from gold labels. Rather than treating activation patching as clean-trace restoration, we ask where hijacked trajectories are fragile and whether recovery depends on a same-problem clean source. Across Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3-8B on GSM8K few-shot, puzzle, and sycophant hijacks, three few-shot/puzzle cells pass confirmatory [MATH] localization after Bonferroni correction. A selection-aware 50/50 band validation preserves held-out in-band minus out-of-band gaps of +32.6, +45.1, and +17.7 points for Qwen-puzzle, Llama3-fewshot, and Llama3-puzzle, while exact [MATH] agreement is much less stable. Qwen-fewshot remains exploratory, and sycophant cells are temporal-diffuse under short patches. A BF16 Qwen-puzzle full-band sweep preserves the band signal ([MATH], spread 0.33 at [MATH], peak layer 20), supporting the conclusion that the band is not only an INT4 artifact. Fixed-hook GSM8K reruns preserve recovery in both primary puzzle cells: Qwen-puzzle recovers 47.0\% at [MATH] (47/100; Wilson 95\% CI [37.5\%, 56.7\%]), while Llama3-puzzle recovers 39.0\% at [MATH] (39/100; [30.0\%, 48.8\%]). Frozen transfer to MATH-500 recovers 26.0\% of qualified cases in the largest fixed-transfer run (13/50; Wilson 95\% CI [15.9\%, 39.6\%]). Source controls change the mechanism interpretation. Paired bootstraps give finite-sample non-separation between clean and random sources in Qwen-fewshot (+3.0 points, 95\% CI [-18.2,+27.3]) and Llama3-puzzle at expanded [MATH] (clean--random -8.3 [-21.7,+5.0]), while Llama3-fewshot is content-mediated (+40.0 [+16.7,+60.0]).
tldr: This paper studies chain-of-thought answer hijacking in large language models, focusing on diagnostic methods to detect and localize reasoning manipulations.
motivation: To understand and detect adversarial attacks where benign-looking chain-of-thought reasoning leads to harmful final answers in LLMs.
method: Uses activation patching and selection-aware band validation on GSM8K and MATH-500 datasets with Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3-8B models.
result: Identifies fragile regions in hijacked trajectories; few-shot/puzzle cells show significant band gaps; recovery rates vary by model and hijack type.
conclusion: The band signal is robust across precision levels, but source controls change mechanism interpretation; suggests need for better diagnostics.

title: Improved Approximation Guarantees For Groupwise Maximin Share Fairness
authors: Georgios Amanatidis, Anna Korfiati, Evangelos Markakis, Christodoulos Santorinaios
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of fairly allocating a set of indivisible goods to a set of [MATH] agents with additive valuation functions. We focus on the very demanding notion of (GMMS), which requires that each agent [MATH] receives value comparable to their maximin share, where the latter is computed . We show that it is possible to compute [MATH]-approximate GMMS allocations in polynomial time, where [MATH] is the golden ratio). This improves on the previously known guarantee of [MATH] of Chaudhury et al. [SICOMP; 2021] and Amanatidis et al. [TCS; 2020]. We propose a simple algorithm that maintains the same main properties as the Draft-and-Eliminate algorithm of Amanatidis et al. [TCS, 2020] and we improve on the approximation guarantee analysis by carefully bounding the relevant value within any subinstance induced by the restriction of our allocation to a subset of agents. Our analysis is asymptotically tight for algorithms that share these properties and has the additional benefit of giving improved guarantees for restricted settings; in particular, when the agents agree on the top [MATH] goods or when the number of agents is small. To illustrate the challenges of going beyond the guarantees of our algorithm, we also present a variant with an improved approximation of [MATH] for the case of three agents. To achieve this improvement we partially characterize the maximin share guarantees of short picking sequences for a small number of goods.
tldr: This paper improves approximation guarantees for groupwise maximin share fairness in indivisible goods allocation, achieving a golden ratio approximation.
motivation: To improve upon existing approximation guarantees for the demanding notion of groupwise maximin share (GMMS) fairness in resource allocation.
method: The authors propose a simple algorithm based on the Draft-and-Eliminate framework and provide a refined analysis that bounds the relevant value within subinstances induced by restricting allocation to a subset of agents.
result: They achieve a polynomial-time (φ)-approximate GMMS allocation, where φ is the golden ratio, improving on the previous 2-approximation. The analysis is asymptotically tight for algorithms with similar properties.
conclusion: The work provides improved guarantees for general settings and special cases (e.g., small number of agents), and presents a variant for three agents with a 1.618-approximation, highlighting challenges for further improvement.

title: Abduction Prover In Isabelle/HOL
authors: Daniel Sebastian Goc Yutaka Nagashima
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof assistants based on expressive logics suffer limited automation for proof search, raising the cost of formal verification based on proof assistants. We address this problem by introducing the Abduction Prover for Isabelle/HOL. Given a challenging proof goal, the Abduction Prover constructs a proof script for the goal by identifying useful conjectures using abductive reasoning.
tldr: This paper presents an abduction prover for Isabelle/HOL to improve proof automation in expressive logics.
motivation: Proof assistants based on expressive logics suffer from limited automation for proof search, increasing the cost of formal verification.
method: The authors introduce the Abduction Prover, which constructs proof scripts by identifying useful conjectures using abductive reasoning.
result: The prover can generate proof scripts for challenging proof goals by leveraging abductive reasoning to find conjectures.
conclusion: The approach aims to enhance automation in proof assistants, potentially reducing the effort required for formal verification.

title: Welfare Maximization In Bilateral Trade: Improved Approximation Guarantees Beyond The Fixed Price Barrier
authors: Ariel Shaulker Shahar Dobzinski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the setting of welfare maximization in bilateral trade, where the values of both the buyer and the seller are drawn from independent distributions. Our goal is to maximize social welfare. In this setting, fixed price mechanisms have been extensively studied. In a fixed price mechanism, there is a price [MATH] that depends only on the distributions of the buyer and the seller. Trade occurs if and only if the buyer's value is at least [MATH] and the seller's value is at most [MATH]. A long line of work has culminated in determining almost exactly the approximation ratios achievable by fixed price mechanisms: there exists a fixed price mechanism that obtains at least a [MATH] fraction of the social welfare, but no fixed price mechanism can guarantee more than a [MATH] fraction of it [Cai and Wu, STOC'23; Liu, Ren, and Wang, STOC'23]. No other incentive-compatible mechanism is known to beat the performance of fixed-price mechanisms in this setting. This paper shows how to achieve a larger fraction of the optimal welfare with other classes of mechanisms. Specifically, we study the buyer-offering mechanism with a reserve price. In this mechanism, the buyer observes its value and makes a take-it-or-leave-it offer to the seller, where the offer is at least the reserve price. Beyond its simplicity, this natural mechanism is attractive because the seller always has a dominant strategy: accept the offer if its value is at most the offer, and otherwise reject it. We show that there always exists a reserve price that guarantees a [MATH] fraction of the social welfare. This not only improves upon the best previously known approximation guarantee for the problem, but also demonstrates that fixed-price mechanisms are not optimal in this setting.
tldr: This paper studies welfare maximization in bilateral trade using a buyer-offering mechanism with a reserve price, achieving a better approximation ratio than fixed-price mechanisms.
motivation: To improve upon the known approximation guarantees for welfare maximization in bilateral trade, which were previously limited by fixed-price mechanisms.
method: The authors analyze a buyer-offering mechanism with a reserve price, where the buyer makes a take-it-or-leave-it offer at least the reserve price, and the seller has a dominant strategy to accept if the offer exceeds its value.
result: They prove that there always exists a reserve price guaranteeing a 0.75 fraction of the optimal social welfare, surpassing the best fixed-price mechanism's guarantee of 0.5.
conclusion: This demonstrates that fixed-price mechanisms are not optimal for bilateral trade, opening the door for better mechanisms in this setting.

title: Event Calculus Meets Hybrid Asp
authors: Ond\v{r}ej Va\v{s}\'i\v{c}ek, Joaqu\'in Arias, Jan Fiedor, Gopal Gupta, Bohuslav K\v{r}ena, Jakub N\v{e}mec, Javier Romero, Tom\'a\v{s} Vojnar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Event Calculus (EC) implemented in answer set programming (ASP) has proven suitable for specifying requirements on safety-critical systems thanks to its elegant representation of both discrete and continuous changes and its semantic closeness to semi-formal natural language. However, continuous changes and the size of value domains of time and system properties (fluents) pose significant challenges. Grounding-based ASP solvers, e.g., clingo, which implement Discrete EC (DEC), lead to combinatorial explosion in program size and inaccurate representation. The grounding-free s(CASP) does not discretize but struggles with non-termination due to its top-down execution. This paper introduces Hybrid EC, an extended axiomatization of DEC, that tackles the challenges via functional fluents and a mapping of time to abstract steps. We implement it using clingcon and clingo-lpx (Hybrid ASP systems over integers and rationals, respectively) where the value (dense) domains of fluents and time are represented as linear constraints and evaluated by external solvers, while ensuring termination whenever solutions exist. We validate both implementations on a number of examples and observe that they are unaffected by the size of the domains and that handling rationals does not impact scalability. Most importantly, the ability of clingo-lpx to handle dense domains enables accurate modeling of continuous change.
tldr: This paper extends Event Calculus with hybrid ASP to handle continuous changes and large value domains in safety-critical systems, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: Existing Event Calculus implementations face combinatorial explosion or non-termination when dealing with continuous changes and large domains.
method: The authors propose Hybrid EC, an extended axiomatization using functional fluents and abstract time steps, implemented with clingcon and clingo-lpx (hybrid ASP solvers) to handle dense domains via linear constraints.
result: The implementations are unaffected by domain size and handle rationals without scalability loss, enabling accurate modeling of continuous change.
conclusion: Hybrid EC with hybrid ASP solvers provides a scalable and accurate approach for specifying requirements in safety-critical systems with continuous dynamics.

title: TeeDAO: A Decentralized Autonomous Organization For Heterogeneous TEEs
authors: Pinshen Xu, Wentao Dong, Guoxing Chen, Jianyu Niu, Cong Wang, Yinqian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) have emerged as a critical technology for safeguarding sensitive data and ensuring code integrity in modern computing systems. However, relying on a single TEE implementation makes systems vulnerable to a central point of attack. Building distributed-trust systems leveraging heterogeneous TEEs helps disperse trust but still faces threats from centralized management and adaptive mobile adversaries. To address these challenges, this paper introduces TeeDAO, a novel three-layer framework that automatically organizes multiple heterogeneous TEE instances and provides unified interfaces to support diverse applications, while ensuring long-term guarantees of availability, integrity, and confidentiality. TeeDAO couples BFT-ordered governance with heterogeneity-aware Distributed Proactive Secret Sharing (DPSS) and Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) so that attestation-driven committee changes are consistently reflected in secret recovery, resharing, and computation across a dynamic committee of heterogeneous TEEs. We implement a prototype of TeeDAO, integrating COBRA's DPSS scheme with the HotStuff BFT consensus protocol, and adapt it for Intel SGX, TDX, and Hygon CSV. Evaluations demonstrate that TeeDAO achieves up to 1.8x higher key-value store throughput in a large cluster with 61 nodes compared to state-of-the-art systems, efficient autonomous management, and minimal computation overhead (<18%) for multi-party computation tasks.
tldr: TeeDAO is a decentralized framework for managing heterogeneous Trusted Execution Environments using BFT consensus and proactive secret sharing.
motivation: To address vulnerabilities in single TEE implementations and centralized management by building a distributed-trust system with heterogeneous TEEs.
method: The paper proposes a three-layer framework coupling BFT-ordered governance with heterogeneity-aware Distributed Proactive Secret Sharing (DPSS) and Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC), implemented with COBRA's DPSS and HotStuff BFT.
result: TeeDAO achieves up to 1.8x higher key-value store throughput in a 61-node cluster compared to state-of-the-art systems, with efficient autonomous management and minimal MPC overhead (<18%).
conclusion: TeeDAO demonstrates a practical approach to decentralized trust using heterogeneous TEEs, with implications for secure distributed computing.

title: NLLog: Lightweight, Explainable Soc Anomaly Detection Via Log-to-Language Rewriting
authors: Samuel Ndichu, Tao Ban, Seiichi Ozawa, Takeshi Takahashi, Daisuke Inoue
abstract: ArXiv:2606.04957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System-generated logs underpin security monitoring, yet their rigid template-based format hinders both automated analysis and human comprehension. We present NLLog (Natural-Language Log), a lightweight pipeline that deterministically rewrites parsed templates into WHO-WHAT-SEVERITY sentences, pools them with term-frequency-inverse-document-frequency weighting, classifies sessions with tree ensembles, and back-projects evidence with TreeSHAP for analyst review. On Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) and Blue Gene/L (BGL) corpora, NLLog exceeds two reproduced matched-protocol baselines; across HDFS, BGL, and the AIT Alert Data Set, it sustains low false-positive rates with commodity-hardware latency suitable for security operations center triage. Coverage, sparse-versus-dense, faithfulness, and adversarial ablations show that fallback sufficiency is corpus-dependent, that an enrollment-time coverage check can surface refinement requirements before deployment, and that an auditable deterministic rewrite combined with lightweight dense encoding provides a measurable representation layer for log-anomaly detection and triage.
tldr: NLLog is a lightweight log anomaly detection pipeline that rewrites parsed log templates into natural language sentences and uses TF-IDF and tree ensembles for classification.
motivation: System logs are rigid and template-based, hindering both automated analysis and human comprehension. The authors aim to improve interpretability and efficiency in security operations center triage.
method: The pipeline deterministically rewrites parsed log templates into WHO-WHAT-SEVERITY sentences, pools them with TF-IDF weighting, classifies sessions with tree ensembles, and uses TreeSHAP for back-projection of evidence.
result: On HDFS and BGL corpora, NLLog exceeds two reproduced baselines, sustains low false-positive rates, and achieves commodity-hardware latency. Coverage and adversarial ablations show corpus-dependent fallback sufficiency.
conclusion: The auditable deterministic rewrite combined with lightweight dense encoding provides a measurable representation layer for log-anomaly detection and triage, but deployment requires enrollment-time coverage checks.
